it_fiat_6616_cockerill: An Italian wheeled light tank that keeps the FIAT 6614's mobility but adds a new, quick-turning turret armed with the low-pressure 90 mm Cockerill Mk.III. Protection is practically absent, to the point that light machine guns can hurt it at close range, so survival depends on speed: on paved ground it moves fast enough to slip out of trouble. Careful positioning, scouting and surprise attacks are what make it work. It was added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_fiat_6616_ub: Somaliland's improvised take on the Fiat and OTO Melara 6616 armoured car: vehicles captured from Somalia, which had ordered 30 with 20 mm MK 20 cannons in 1977, were fitted around 2014 with aircraft UB-16-57UMP rocket pods fixed to the turret roof. A 100 km/h top speed makes it a quick scout and flanker, and the 20 mm handles light vehicles and can break barrels or tracks, but heavy armour defeats it. Because the rocket pod cannot elevate, it is only dependable at point-blank range, and the crew has almost no armour around them. It was a Battle Pass Season XXIV "Do It Yourself" reward.
it_fiat_cm52: The Fiat 6601 ACM 52 "Quadrinata" is an Italian wheeled anti-aircraft vehicle carrying the Maxson M45 mount with four 12.7 mm M2 machine guns, which puts it in the same family as the American M13 and M16 GMCs. It is a strong anti-air choice for its tier, and road speed lets it relocate often so aircraft struggle to pin it down; thinly armoured ground targets can also fall to it. Its weak points are the lack of armour and limited gun depression over the front. It joined the game in the "Apex Predators" update.
it_freccia: Built by Iveco and OTO Melara on the basis of the Centauro family, the Freccia infantry fighting vehicle entered Italian service in 2009 to replace the ageing VCC-2 carriers. Its turret carries Spike fire-and-forget missiles with modest penetration that fly erratically up close, so it suits long-range sniping. The tall hull is hard to hide, yet the armour shrugs off light autocannon fire; it is fast on roads but slows in mud and snow. Spikes can lock aircraft but are slow, so the IRST-guided cannon is the better anti-air tool. It came with the "La Royale" update.
it_freccia_hitfist_ows: The newest Freccia variant swaps the manned turret for the remote Hitfist OWS, armed with a 30 mm Bushmaster 2 and a twin Spike launcher; the Italian Army plans to buy around 300 with this turret. Against the original Freccia, the unmanned turret makes it a little harder to knock out, and the 30 mm penetrates better than the old 25 mm KBA at the cost of fire rate and ammunition count. Armour is thin, but strong mobility lets it relocate, flank and back up teammates. It was added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
it_kf_41: Rheinmetall's Lynx infantry fighting vehicle was ordered by Hungary in seven variants, 209 vehicles in all, built at a plant in Zalaegerszeg with the first handed over in July 2024. As big and heavy as the Puma, it plays differently: instead of an unmanned turret, ERA/NERA and soft-kill protection, it relies on the AMAP-ADS hard-kill system and plenty of smoke, leaving it exposed to anything that system cannot stop. Spike missiles, APFSDS and an excellent commander's sight make it a strong long-range scout and point defender, while 30 mm AHEAD shells help against helicopters. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update with the Hungarian branch of the Italian tree.
it_l3_cc: Ansaldo's L3/33 tankette (Carro Veloce) served the Royal Italian Army from 1933 in Yugoslavia, Albania and Greece; this CC version mounts a 20 mm Fucile Controcarri S Mod.39 anti-tank rifle, and some lasted into post-war police service. Being tiny, it tucks easily into foliage or behind bushes and works best as an ambusher. Good mobility lets it scout and dart into flanking spots against slower, heavier opponents. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_l6: Ansaldo's L6/40 light tank of the 1940s reworked the L3 chassis, keeping a two-man crew while improving firepower, armour and mobility, and saw heavy use during the occupation of the Balkans. Its 20 mm Breda Mod.35, which can fire the German PzGr 40 among other rounds, copes well with the lightly armoured opponents it mostly meets, and the turret turns quickly. Mobility is acceptable, but survivability is poor: thin plating and a cramped crew layout mean one good hit often finishes it, so it does best staying near sturdier teammates. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_l6_leone: This L6/40 represents the tanks of the Italian 31st Regiment, which fought guerrillas in the Balkans, chiefly in Albania in 1942–43, and guarded infrastructure in occupied Yugoslavia; it wears the regiment's painted lion mascot. In play it matches the standard L6/40: the 20 mm Breda autocannon and fast turret traverse are enough for most lightly armoured foes, and mobility is adequate. Protection is the problem, as thin armour and close-packed crew mean a single well-aimed shot can end it, so it is safer operating behind heavier allies. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_lancia3ro_100: The Lancia 3Ro heavy truck, roughly 9,490 of which were built during the war, was sometimes turned into a makeshift self-propelled gun by removing the cab roof and mounting a 100/17 howitzer, seeing use in North Africa and Sicily. As a truck conversion it has middling mobility and almost no protection. The stock HE and AP shells are weak, but the researchable HEAT round, with around 110 mm of penetration, lets it destroy anything it usually meets. Its fragility means it is best kept behind cover or teammates in a supporting role. It came in the "Danger Zone" update.
it_leopard_1a2: Italy bought 200 German-built Leopard 1s in 1971–72 to replace its M47s, then licence-built 520 more A2s at OTO Melara between 1974 and 1983; this variant added stronger turret armour and passive night vision. They served on Balkan peacekeeping missions without ever seeing combat and left service in 2003. In the game it keeps the Leopard's speed and hard-hitting gun, but the armour is thin and there is neither a stabiliser nor a laser rangefinder, so it rewards cautious, deliberate play. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
it_leopard_1a5: Italy's Leopard 1A5 was a hybrid, combining a licence-built hull from the Leopard 1A2 family with the 1A5 turret after a home-grown fire-control upgrade was passed over; it served mainly with the KFOR mission. The thermal sight and good zoom suit it to sniping, and its 105 mm L7A3 with APFSDS can defeat nearly every opponent it meets. Stock mobility is sluggish until modules arrive, and the armour is weak enough for IFV cannons to penetrate, with a large ammunition store in the front hull; a laser warning receiver, missing on the German version, helps a little. It arrived in the "New Power" update.
it_leopard_2a4: Hungary received 12 refurbished Leopard 2A4s from KMW in 2020 for crew training alongside its Leopard 2A7HU order; designated 2A4HU, they serve with the 25th Infantry Brigade and the 11th Tank Battalion. In the game it differs from the German 2A4 only in camouflage and is among the most well-rounded tanks of its rank: fast and agile, with a quick-firing 120 mm Rh 120 L/44, reasonable composite armour and turret blow-out panels. Loading more than 16 rounds puts shells in the front hull, where powerful APFSDS and tandem missiles can reach them. It came in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila" as part of the Italian tree.
it_leopard_2a7_hungary: Built for Hungary under a 2018 contract for 44 tanks, the Leopard 2A7HU develops the 2A7+ with improved turret protection, a PERI RTWL commander's sight, a newer fire-control system and provision for a remote 12.7 mm M2 weapon station. It brings a well-protected turret, high-resolution thermal sights for both gunner and commander, and a 120 mm gun whose DM53 APFSDS defeats heavy armour. The drawback is weight: with the "Mine protection" modification fitted it reaches 67 tonnes, which noticeably dulls its speed and agility. It was introduced in Update 2.37 "Active Search" in the Italian ground tree.
it_leopard_bofors: The Leopard 40/70 was an Italian anti-aircraft prototype of the late 1990s, meant to work alongside the SIDAM 25 covering armoured columns; the army trialled it for years but never put it into production. Dropping the Leopard's gun turret saved enough weight to make it one of the most mobile vehicles of its tier, and the Breda Bofors 40 mm works against both ground and air targets, elevating far enough to engage aircraft directly overhead. Thin armour and exposed crew mean almost anything can kill it in one shot, so hit-and-run flanking with frequent moves suits it best. It was added in the "Kings of Battle" update.
it_m109g: Italy obtained the American M109 self-propelled howitzer to follow its post-war M44s, upgrading some to M109L standard with an OTO Melara 155 mm gun and a rammer; the type served on peacekeeping operations until the PzH 2000 replaced it in the early 2000s. Armour is minimal, and even 14.5 mm machine guns or light autocannons can get through. The 155 mm HE shell is its strength, able to overpressure or penetrate most tanks, with turret roofs and hull bottoms the targets on heavies. A long reload and slow turret make ambushing alongside allies, then pulling back to reload, the usual approach. It was added in the "Kings of Battle" update.
it_m113a1_tow: OTO Melara's version of the M113A1 carrier, here armed with a TOW anti-tank missile launcher. On a suitable map the TOW is very dangerous, and the launcher sits high enough that the hull can stay behind cover while only the missile pokes out to pick off distant targets; bushes help with concealment. There is no real armour, so machine guns go straight through, and the exposed missile operator is at the mercy of aircraft and artillery. It is nimble for its size and keeps pace with the team. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m11_39: Italy's first home-designed tank grew out of a programme begun in 1932 and entered production in 1939; 100 were built and fought in East and North Africa until 1942, when weak armour, an awkward layout, a poor gun and a shortage of spares retired them. Its lessons fed directly into the M13/40 and M14/41. In the game it holds up well under fire, moves decently and has an adequate gun, so it can ambush or push. Thin sides, a narrow firing arc and mediocre ballistics make open ground its enemy. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m13_40_serie_1: The M13/40 answered the M11/39's flaws with a proper turret mounting a stronger 47 mm gun and a fourth crewman to load it, on a new Ansaldo hull reusing the old running gear; it was adopted in 1940, and this first series numbered 100 tanks. In the game it is a breakthrough tank: when angled, its armour shrugs off a lot of fire, and the gun can kill or cripple targets in one shot up close. Reloading is slow, mobility mediocre, and beyond roughly 500 m the shells lose enough penetration to become unreliable. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic", with the (II) and (III) series following as improvements.
it_m13_40_serie_2: The second M13/40 production run of 200 tanks gained a higher gun elevation limit, a radio antenna, short track guards and other small changes. It was first handed out as a battle reward during the 2018 War Thunder Festivities in Update 1.85 "Supersonic" and has since been sold for Golden Eagles. Compared with the first series it fires faster and has better aiming angles, backed by decent armour and a good gun. The turret still turns slowly, and weak acceleration makes its modest 32 km/h top speed hard to reach.
it_m13_40_serie_3: The third and largest M13/40 batch, with 410 tanks built, added a raised rectangular section on the turret roof to ease gun handling, among other refinements. It shares the (II)'s quicker fire rate and better gun angles, and like the rest of the family it can lead pushes: angled armour deflects much enemy fire, and close-range shots often destroy or disable targets outright. Past about 500 m the shells struggle to penetrate, and the slow turret and middling mobility remain. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m14_41: A reworked M13/40 aimed at problems found in North Africa, the M14/41 got a more powerful engine, extra fuel and air filters and better electrics; about 750 were made from 1941 to 1943, the first by converting M13/40s. It fought in North Africa and in the defence of Italy, and some ended up with the Allies and the Wehrmacht. In battle it is quick, fires rapidly and carries a respectable gun, but its tall silhouette, middling armour and slow turret hold it back. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m14_41_47_40: A one-off wartime experiment, this M14/41 swapped its 47/32 gun for the longer 47/40 of the M15/42 and replaced the twin 8 mm Breda Model 31 machine guns with one 13.2 mm Breda Model 38, a pairing previously limited to command tanks and tankettes. It turned up near Milan in the 1950s, but its service and fate are unknown. Light weight and a thin hull make it play more like a light tank, and narrow tracks hurt it on soft ground. The longer gun penetrates better than the original, the 13.2 mm handles light vehicles, and the turret is fairly well armoured. It was added in Update 1.99.1 "Regina Marina".
it_m15_42: The M15/42 was the last refinement of the Fiat-Ansaldo M13/40 line, begun in mid-1942 with a 190 hp petrol engine, chosen because diesel was reserved for the navy and freight, and an improved 47/32 gun. Only 152 were built, serving the Royal Italian Army, the Wehrmacht and, after September 1943, the Salò republic's army, and its hull also underpinned the Semovente 75/18 and 75/34. In the game it is mobile and reloads its decent gun quickly, but thin armour and a slow-turning gun keep it from shining. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m15_42_contraereo: Ordered in 1942 to protect North African columns from RAF attack, the Semovente Contraereo da 20/70 quadruplo put an open polygonal turret with four 20 mm Scotti Isotta Fraschini guns on the M15/42 hull. The prototype entered service in March 1943, fell into German hands in Rome and was still in use with an SS corps near Teupitz in April 1945. Much like the German Wirbelwind, and sharing ammunition with German 20 mm guns, it brings down even heavy aircraft in a few hits, making it one of Italy's best low-rank anti-aircraft vehicles. The crew is poorly protected, so fire only when hits are likely. It came in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m18_hellcat: Italy received 130 surplus American M18 tank destroyers by July 1952, delivered without their side skirts and issued to the 155th Artillery Regiment near the eastern border until M47s and other tanks replaced them in the early 1960s. Compared with the American original it lacks the M93 shell, but the 76 mm M1 with APCBC still hits hard and mobility remains excellent. That suits flanking and grabbing key positions early. Thin armour and an open-topped turret leave it vulnerable to a wide range of threats. It was added in Update 1.99 "Starfighters".
it_m24_chaffee: Italy received 518 American M24 light tanks through the Mutual Defense Assistance Program and used them from the early 1950s with cavalry, armoured and Bersaglieri units, later moving them to reconnaissance and, by about 1970, training; three survive in Italian museums. In the game it is quick, reaching 56 km/h forward, and carries a good gun, but its armour stops little of what it meets. It therefore works as a flanker or sniper rather than a front-line brawler. It was introduced in Update 1.99 "Starfighters".
it_m26_ariete: Supplied by the US under the Mutual Defense Assistance Act in the early 1950s to replace worn-out Shermans, these M26 Pershings went to the 132nd Armoured Division "Ariete", reformed in 1948 and posted near the Yugoslav border, and never saw combat. The tank is large and easy to catch from hidden angles in tight urban maps, and it is slow until mobility modules are researched, so early on it suits a support role. Its armour stops many medium-calibre shells, especially hull-down, and the 90 mm Cannone da 90/50 M3A1 kills most opponents in one or two hits when aimed at weak spots. It was introduced in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
it_m26a1_pershing: Italy's M26A1 Pershings came from the US in the early 1950s under the Mutual Defense Assistance Act, replacing obsolete Shermans and becoming one of the army's strongest tanks for years. Playing it means managing a big, slow tank: it is an easy target for unseen enemies in close urban fighting and needs mobility upgrades before it can lead an attack. Hull-down, its armour resists many medium-calibre rounds, and the 90 mm M3A1 gun can kill most enemies in one or two shots if aimed at weak points, with machine guns for light vehicles. It came in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m36b1: The M36B1 was the second production series of the American M36 tank destroyer, built on the M4A3 tank hull; Italy received 36 of them after joining NATO in 1949 to bolster around six tank battalions. Against the standard M36 it has a sturdier hull, a better-penetrating gun and access to APCR, including the improved M332, plus HEAT, while the M82 APCBC does heavy damage after penetrating. Mobility is mediocre, reversing especially, and the open turret leaves it exposed to aircraft and artillery. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m3a3_stuart: Post-war Italy received American M3A3 Stuarts through the Military Assistance Program, and their compact size suited Italian terrain and doctrine well enough that they served with armoured regiments for decades. In the game, strong mobility lets it seize a capture point or a good position early, and its small size makes it easy to hide for ambushes. The crew layout is unforgiving, so one solid hit often ends its fight. The gun handles other light tanks, and heavier targets are reachable through their sides, which its speed makes easy to get at. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
it_m44: Italy took delivery of 105 American M44 self-propelled howitzers in 1957, a big step up from towed guns; they served with units including the "Brennero" and "Avisio" artillery groups until the M109G replaced them, and nearly all had left front-line units by 1986. Compact and reasonably mobile, it carries a powerful 155 mm gun with M107 HE and M110 smoke shells. The thin hull and open-topped fighting compartment make it easy prey for tanks and aircraft alike, the gun's horizontal arc is limited to 30 degrees, and the long reload makes it far better at range than up close. It came in the "Storm Warning" update.
it_m47_105: In the 1970s OTO Melara proposed re-arming Italy's M47s, received in large numbers from 1952, with a 105 mm gun derived from the L7 but given a redesigned breech and a 55-calibre barrel to avoid royalties, plus the M60's diesel engine and an infrared-suppression system; the army bought new M60s instead. In the game the diesel gives it good mobility, and the L7-based gun with a fast reload and middling armour make it a capable spearhead. Against that, it is large, has numerous weak spots including in the turret front, and its gun is very slow to lay onto targets. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_m4a4_sherman: The M4A4 was the fifth model of the early Sherman family, and post-war American aid gave the new Italian Army at least 57 M4A2s and M4A4s combined, which served as its main medium tanks from 1948 until the last were retired in 1952. Its armour layout matches other early Shermans, with hull hatches bulging out of the sloped front plate; welded add-on plates only partly cover these spots, and experienced opponents aim for them. The Chrysler multibank engine, assembled from five car engines, required the hull to be lengthened by 15 cm. It was introduced in the "Starfighters" update.
it_m55: Italy received 24 American M55 self-propelled howitzers in 1960 and retired them in the late 1970s; little else is recorded of their service. Firepower is its only real asset: the 203 mm M47 howitzer throws an HE shell with about 23 kg of TNT equivalent that destroys any tank in the game if placed well. With only ten rounds aboard and a very long reload, every miss is costly, leaving the large, thinly armoured hull exposed to return fire. It was added in the "Tusk Force" update.
it_m60a1_ariete: Italy ordered the M60A1 in 1965 to replace its M47s, buying 100 from the US and licence-building 200 more at OTO Melara; this one represents the 132nd Armoured Division "Ariete", Italy's first large armoured formation, created in 1939 and today a brigade. It is the American M60A1 (AOS) with distinct camouflage and no stabiliser, which makes firing on the move hard when many opponents can. Protection is decent and the 105 mm gun is good, though top speed is unremarkable. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_of_40_mk_1: OTO Melara's OF-40, often seen as Italy's first post-war attempt at a main battle tank, drew on experience from the Leone project, itself a modified Leopard I. It plays much like the German Leopard 1 series: slightly better turret armour but the same weak spots, good mobility and a strong 105 mm gun. The gun is unstabilised, so stopping to fire works best, and while a laser rangefinder is fitted there is no thermal sight. Played around those limits it is quite effective. It was added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_of_40_mk_2a: The Mk.2A upgrade gave OTO Melara's OF-40 a low-light television camera and a stabilised gun. That stabiliser is the key change in the game, letting its 105 mm fire accurately on the move with APFSDS, HEAT and HESH; the laser rangefinder stays and night vision is added, though there is still no thermal sight. Armour remains a touch better than the Leopard I's yet shares its weak spots, and mobility keeps pace with most tanks it meets. It came in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_of_40_mtca: Built on OTO Melara's OF-40 Mk.2A, the MTCA variant swaps in a 1,000 hp Fiat MTCA V-12 engine for much better mobility. It reaches key positions faster than most rivals of its tier, rewarding aggressive play and flanking, but keeps the earlier OF-40s' weak spots and has night vision rather than thermals. It wears a unique skin based on the OF-40s exported to the UAE. Added in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy", it left the Gaijin store after the May 2022 sale and returned as a Golden Eagle premium in the "Danger Zone" update.
it_oto_r3_106sr: The OTO Melara R3 Capraia was a light reconnaissance vehicle aimed mainly at export and also trialled by the Italian Army for the Folgore regiment; at least seven prototypes existed with different weapons, but a crowded market meant none were ordered. This version carries twin American 106 mm recoilless rifles firing HEAT and HESH, which together with high road speed make it a hard-hitting, nimble tank hunter and a capable scout. It lacks smoke, a stabiliser, night vision and thermals, the armour is weak, and it handles poorly in turns and on snow or mud. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_oto_r3_t20_fa: Another member of OTO Melara's R3 Capraia family, an export-oriented scout car that reached prototype stage and was trialled by the Italian Army but never ordered. This anti-aircraft version mounts a 20 mm Oerlikon KAD cannon that shreds light vehicles and can break barrels and engines on heavier ones, while generous elevation makes it effective against aircraft, especially WW2 types. Speed is the standout trait, letting it pounce on targets or rush capture points, but it has weak armour, no smoke, twitchy handling in turns and trouble on snow or mud. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_otobreda_sidam_25: OTO Melara's SIDAM 25 put four 25 mm Oerlikon KBA cannons on the M113A1 chassis, chosen over the costlier OTOMATIC despite having no radar; 275 were ordered, and most were later stripped to supply 25 mm guns for the Freccia. Its dense fire brings down aircraft and helicopters in seconds, helped by fast HEI-T shells, and once the M791 APDS belt is researched it gains about 81 mm of penetration, putting tanks on the menu. The 660 rounds last only around 18 seconds of firing, the large hull is hard to conceal, and heavy machine guns go through the armour, so staying hidden and firing selectively is key. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_otobreda_sidam_25_mistral: A single prototype, this SIDAM 25 was fitted with Mistral surface-to-air missiles as OTO Melara's last attempt to keep the radar-less, M113-based gun system relevant. It keeps the quad 25 mm Oerlikon KBA mount, which shreds aircraft with HEI-T and, once the APDS belt is researched, threatens tanks too, though 660 rounds empty in about 18 seconds of fire. The six Mistrals add reach against low-flying aircraft and helicopters, but countermeasures can defeat them, so launching while the target is distracted or alongside cannon fire works better. Like the gun-only version it is large and poorly armoured. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
it_otomatic: OTO Melara's OTOMATIC of the late 1980s, part of its OF-40/Palmaria family, mounted an adapted 76 mm naval gun with search and tracking radar, a datalink and a dedicated APFSDS round, but Italy found it too expensive and bought the simpler SIDAM 25. Its proximity-fused shells can down an aircraft with one good hit, though only 90 rounds are carried and jets and helicopters often outrange it, so patience and concealment matter. Once APFSDS is researched, the autoloader makes it dangerous to tanks from the flank. It is large and thinly armoured, an easy ATGM target, but mobile for its type. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_p_26_40: The P40 "G.C. Leoncello" was one of the first Italian ground vehicles in the game, created by community members Nicola "Kolin0" Faggiani and Riccardo "BlueBeta" Lo Verso through the revenue-sharing programme. Its performance is middle of the road in every respect, with armour, gun and mobility all average, so it fits flanking or support roles but should not be relied on as a shield or for speed. Its standard camouflage is a three-tone yellow, green and red-brown scheme. It was sold as a premium pack from Update 1.73 "Vive la France" until the May 2020 sale, and briefly returned for Golden Eagles during the 2021 Italian National Unity Day event.
it_p_40: Italy's P26/40 began in 1940 as a heavy infantry tank to back up the mediums against better-armed Allied tanks; its gun grew from a 75/18 to a 75/34, the design gained sloped plates, and at 26 tonnes it counted as heavy by Italian standards. Only five were completed before the 1943 armistice, after which Germany built around a hundred more, many used as engineless fixed strongpoints. In the game it strikes a balance: APCBC and HEAT shells defeat almost anything it faces, mobility is middling, and it can absorb some punishment. It arrived with the first Italian ground tree in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_palmaria: OTO Melara began the Palmaria in 1977, putting a 155 mm howitzer in a turret on the export OF-40 chassis; production ran from 1982 to 1990, with Libya and Nigeria taking 187 and Argentina fitting 25 turrets to TAM hulls. Libyan government forces used it effectively in the civil war until NATO precision bombs destroyed many. In the game it is big, thinly armoured and fragile but fairly quick, and its HE shells can kill with one well-placed hit, helped by a mechanised ammunition rack that keeps the reload respectable. A proximity-fused shell also works against aircraft. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
it_pzh_2000: Italy chose the German Panzerhaubitze 2000 to replace its ageing M109Ls, with an OTO Melara-led consortium licence-building 70 between 2004 and 2008; six were later given to Ukraine in 2022. Automatic loading lets the 155 mm gun fire quickly for its size, and with excellent ballistics and a laser rangefinder it is very effective at medium and long range, while the chassis gets it into position fast. It is weakly protected, large and slow to traverse. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
it_pzh_2000_hu: Hungary ordered 24 PzH 2000s from KMW in December 2018 to replace its Soviet-era towed D-20 howitzers; the first arrived in August 2022, destined for the 101st Tata Artillery Division in support of the 1st György Klapka Armoured Brigade. In the game the autoloaded 155 mm gun fires fast for its calibre and, with fine ballistics and a laser rangefinder, excels from medium to long range, while good mobility helps it reach firing spots. Weak protection, a big silhouette and slow turret traverse are the trade-offs. It was introduced in the "Storm Warning" update.
it_pzkpfw_III_ausf_N: Germany sent Pz.III Ns to the Italian Social Republic in 1943, and 12 equipped the second company of the 1st Armoured Division Black Shirts "M"; the division was still training when the Germans took them back, and they were later captured by the Allies. In the game it is the German Pz.III N minus the side skirts, leaving the flanks slightly more exposed, and without the commander's cupola machine gun. Its HEAT shell tops out at about 100 mm of penetration, so aiming for weak spots pays off. It arrived in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
it_pzkpfw_IV_ausf_G: Twelve late-production Pz.IV Gs, among the last built before the H, went to the first company of the Italian Social Republic's 1st Armoured Division Black Shirts "M" in 1943; they never fought while the division trained and passed back to German hands before the Allies captured them. Compared with the German version it has extra turret protection and a longer gun, which handles any target it meets. Smoke grenades help it break contact, confuse enemies or cover an attack, and decent speed and acceleration get it to good firing positions or capture points. It arrived in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
it_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_e_tiger: Hungary received 13 to 15 Tiger Es from Germany in 1944 for its 2nd Armoured Division, replacing Turáns that could not cope with the T-34-85; after failed ambushes against the Soviet advance, the survivors broke down for lack of supplies and were destroyed by their own crews. In the game the 88 mm KwK 36 threatens most tanks at any range and the turret is very tough, though the hull front is comparatively easy to penetrate even with its extra armour. A cupola machine gun can fend off aircraft, but air attack remains a danger. Overall it is as dependable as the German Tiger E. It was added in the "Air Superiority" update.
it_sahariano: After meeting British cruiser tanks in North Africa in 1941, Italy designed the Celere Sahariano to match them, copying the Christie suspension from a captured A13 Cruiser Mk III; the 13-tonne prototype had a 275 hp SPA petrol engine good for 55 km/h, and the project died when the Axis left Africa in May 1943. In the game, steeply sloped armour all round makes poorly aimed shots bounce, and with excellent mobility it can flank early and raid the enemy's rear. Its gun is the weak link, struggling against well-armoured targets and at long range. It came in the "New Power" update.
it_samp_t_fcs: The SAMP/T "Mamba" from the Franco-Italian Eurosam consortium brought the Aster 30 missile ashore in the early 2010s on truck chassis, Iveco in Italy's case; Italy bought six systems to replace its HAWK batteries. This is the command vehicle of the in-game system, carrying the ARABEL radar that detects targets out to 80 km and tracks up to ten at once, with two missile launchers making up the rest. It has no armour and no weapons, and losing the radar takes the whole system out, so it must be well hidden. It was introduced in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
it_samp_t_launcher: These are the missile launchers of the Franco-Italian SAMP/T "Mamba", Eurosam's land-based use of the Aster 30 that entered service in the early 2010s; Italy's six systems ride on Iveco trucks and replaced HAWK batteries. Two launchers come with the radar vehicle, need no separate research and are operated through it. Their Aster 30s combine active radar homing with inertial guidance and datalink, and are agile missiles able to reach distant targets. The launchers have no protection, are very large and cannot fight ground targets, so keeping them behind cover is essential. They were introduced in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
it_semovente_breda_501: Breda built a single Semovente Controcarro 501 prototype after a 1942 requirement for a better-protected, faster successor to the gun trucks used in North Africa; its 90 mm gun impressed in testing, but the 1943 armistice ended the programme. In the game the gun is strong even when stock, and its best researched shell gives it real one-shot potential. Speed lets it reach ambush positions before both allies and enemies. The open top and lack of armour leave the crew so exposed that machine guns alone can kill it. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_l40: About 400 of these Fiat-Ansaldo tank destroyers were built from 1941 to 1945, placing a 47/32 gun in an open box superstructure on the L6/40 chassis. It was Italy's most heavily armed vehicle on the Eastern Front but already outdated against medium tanks when it arrived; Germany took over the survivors after the armistice, passing some to Croatia and the Slovene Home Guard. In the game the light chassis gives it good mobility and excellent gun depression for hull-down fighting, but the weak gun needs precise shots at weak spots. Thin armour and an open top mean strafing aircraft, or almost anything else, can kill it. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m41_75_18: Inspired by German StuG III use in France, Fiat-Ansaldo and artillery colonel Sergio Berlesi mounted the 75/18 mountain howitzer in the M13/40 hull; the prototype was shown in winter 1941, an initial order of sixty followed, and later versions on the M14/41 and M15/42 brought the total to 476. In the game it moves decently and fires hard-hitting shells, but its armour is unremarkable and the gun's ballistics are poor, which limits it at longer ranges. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m41_75_32: Because the 75/18 M41 relied on short-range HEAT shells to fight Allied armour, the Italian Army in 1943 re-armed some of them with the 75/32 Modello 37 anti-tank gun, a lengthened 75/18; only about 20 were converted before the 75/34 M42 took over. They served with the Ariete II division and then with the Wehrmacht after the armistice. In the game it is a small vehicle with a good gun and HEAT ammunition, but it has thin armour, worse mobility than its relatives, a slow reload and no machine gun for light targets or obstacles. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m41m_90: The Semovente da 90/53 mounted a 90 mm gun adapted from an anti-aircraft weapon at the rear of a stretched M14/41 hull, meant for infantry support and killing Allied tanks; it first fought during the Sicily landings, but numbers were too small to matter. In the game the gun can kill anything it meets, but mobility is limited, so it works best as a low-profile sniper or ambusher. Limited ammunition and a slow reload mean picking targets carefully. Armour is minimal, hits around the gun often kill the crew, and the open rear exposes crew and ammunition even to machine guns, so being flanked is usually fatal. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m42_75_34: Fiat was asked for a self-propelled gun that could fight Allied armour without relying on the short-ranged HEAT of the 75/18 M41; the result, on the M15/42 hull, entered service in April 1943 with a 75/34 mod. 39 gun comparable in power to the Soviet F-34. It saw little action beyond the defence of Rome in 1943, and the Germans seized 36 for use in the Balkans; 165 were built in all. In the game the gun is excellent and mobility decent, but the armour is poor, the crew is packed into a cramped compartment, and the hull-mounted gun's narrow arc holds it back. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m43_105: Fiat-Ansaldo and OTO answered a mid-1942 call for a vehicle that could both support infantry and fight tanks with the Semovente 105/25 M43, shown in February 1943; over 800 were planned, but Italy's weakened industry managed only about 120 by 1944, serving Italian and German units. In the game it packs a lot of firepower into a compact, low body, enough to threaten contemporaries and newer opponents alike. The 105 mm gun's ballistics are mediocre, so it is happiest at medium range, such as in towns. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m43_105_leoncello: This 105/25 M43 wears the camouflage of the Gruppo Squadroni Corazzati "Leoncello" but is otherwise the standard version of Italy's 1943 self-propelled gun, of which roughly 120 were built against a plan for more than 800. It brings strong firepower in a small, hard-to-hit package that can hurt contemporaries and later tanks alike. The 105 mm gun's ballistics are only fair, so medium-range fights, especially on urban maps, play to its strengths. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m43_75_34: With Allied bombing halting gun production in German-occupied Italy, the Germans had the M43 self-propelled guns finished with whatever was on hand, Italian 75/34 Mod. S.F. guns, while thickening the frontal armour; 29 were built and served the Wehrmacht until the war's end. In the game it is a small vehicle with good front armour and a gun that can fire HEAT. Its compact layout leaves it fragile once penetrated, and its shells sometimes lack the penetration needed. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_semovente_m43_75_46: The 75/46 M43 came from German-Italian efforts to fix the 105/25 M43, whose howitzer proved heavy, hard to load and short on penetration, by fitting the German PaK 40 instead; slow output of licensed guns meant only seven were completed, and some were sent to Germany and took part in the defence of Berlin in 1945. In the game it compares with the Jagdpanzer IV: low, mobile and armed with a powerful 75 mm. Its 6 km/h reverse, thin roof and restricted gun arcs hurt, and while the front looks decent, its two 60 mm plates are readily penetrated with crew and ammunition packed behind them. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_sherman_75_37: Chrysler built 1,676 of these hybrid Shermans between August 1943 and January 1944, pairing a welded M4 hull with an M4A1-style cast front, which led many records to mistake them for M4A1s; the British called them Sherman I Hybrid. Some reached Italy after 1945 and joined the small post-war territorial defence force. In the game it is Italy's first dependable foreign medium, with a 75 mm M3 in a fully rotating turret and a wide choice of ammunition. The curved cast front protects reasonably against smaller guns, making it a solid all-rounder. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
it_sherman_VII: This Firefly pairs the 17-pounder turret of the Sherman VC with an M4 Hybrid hull instead of the usual M4A4, a rare combination that served mostly with the Italian Army; how much it fought in WW2 is unclear. Britain passed such tanks to Italy after the war, where, as the M4 Tipo IC Composito, they helped form the first post-war tank training school before all Shermans were retired in 1952. In the game the 76 mm QF 17-pounder is a big step up from the 75 mm M3 of earlier Italian Shermans, though unlike the Sherman VC it gets no APDS. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_sherman_vc_firefly: The Sherman VC was the British Firefly conversion of the M4A4, a stopgap that put the 76 mm QF 17-pounder into a Sherman and became one of the deadliest Allied tanks of its time. Britain handed some to Italy after the war, where they equipped the new territorial defence command and the first post-war tank school until all Shermans were withdrawn in 1952. In the game it is the first big firepower jump over Italy's 75 mm Shermans, and its APDS shells keep it competitive against more advanced opponents for a long stretch of the tree. It arrived in the "Starfighters" update.
it_stug_III_ausf_G: Twelve StuG III Gs equipped the third company of the Italian Social Republic's 1st Armoured Division Black Shirts "M" in 1943, distinguished by removed side skirts and smoke launchers on both sides; they never saw combat during training and returned to German control before the Allies captured them. In the game it mirrors the German StuG III G apart from those changes, with two triple smoke dischargers useful for escaping or confusing opponents. The powerful gun can destroy anything it meets, so a well-protected firing position lets it rack up kills. It was added in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
it_t_72m1: Hungary received 178 Soviet T-72M1s in 1979; they never fought and went into reserve as Leopard 2s replaced them in the 2020s, with some passed on to countries needing to restock Soviet-type tanks. In the game, slow gun traverse and limited speed are its main faults, but used carefully it can spearhead attacks where lower-tier tanks struggle to answer it. It came in the "Sons of Attila" update as part of the Hungarian branch of the Italian tree.
it_toldi_II_a: Named after the Hungarian folk hero Miklós Toldi, the Toldi line began as a development of the Swedish Landsverk L-60; the Toldi II added armour, and 80 were converted to IIA standard with a 40 mm 37/42M gun to fight Soviet forces on the Eastern Front. That extra armour lets it hold its ground better than its Swedish relatives, though it shares some of their weaknesses. A premium Hungarian light tank in the Italian tree, it was the reward for Battle Pass Season III "Strength athletics" during the "Ixwa Strike" update.
it_vbc_pt2: The Freccia traces back to the VBC programme of the 1980s and 1990s, when Italy explored new roles for the Centauro; revived by Iveco and OTO Melara in the late 2000s, it produced this second prototype, carrying the Dardo's TC-25 Hitfist turret but no missiles. In the game it is a fast all-rounder whose roomy hull sometimes lets shells pass through harmlessly. The 25 mm Oerlikon fires several shell types including APFSDS, backed by thermals, night vision and good gun angles, and it can engage aircraft that come close. It is too big to hide well, can struggle off-road, and before key modules are researched it is safest following heavier allies. It came in the "Danger Zone" update.
it_vcc_80_hitfist_30: The VCC-80/30, or "Dardo II", was a pre-series Dardo prototype with a HITFIST turret resembling the Bradley's and a 30 mm Bushmaster II; it matched or beat the 25 mm version in trials, but the army chose the cheaper, simpler domestic option, and its turret later went to a 60 mm fire-support prototype. In the game it has two fixed launchers for TOW-2, TOW-2A and TOW-2B missiles, a flat-shooting 30 mm with effective ammunition, good off-road speed and modern fire control. As with most IFVs it is easily damaged, and the cannon alone is rarely enough against tanks head-on. It was introduced in Update 2.11 "Ground Breaking".
it_vcc_80_hitfist_60: Built because the Italian Army wanted a mix of 25 mm and 60 mm armed IFVs, the VCC-80/60 prototype carries the OTO 60 mm high-velocity gun, which grew out of a joint project with Israel's IMI before the partners went separate ways. An autoloader feeds APFSDS, HE and proximity-fused HE-VT rounds, the last making it dangerous to helicopters hovering a few kilometres away. Armour is thin, though the turret sometimes stops rounds, and mobility is average, lagging until the engine upgrade is researched. Thermals and night vision help it spot enemies. It came in the "Winged Lions" update.
it_vrcc_centauro: The VRCC is the Spanish Army's Centauro, built in Italy and delivered from 2000 with a revised frontal armour layout and smoke launchers like the second-series Centauro; a 2002 follow-on order added some Spanish production of components, an upgraded fire-control system with a better gunner's thermal sight, and a second roof machine gun. In the game this premium's main gain over early Centauros is the DM33 round, penetrating up to 400 mm, along with the later smoke launchers, but protection is barely improved. It carries the markings of Spain's 8th Light Cavalry Regiment "Lusitania" and was introduced in Update 2.19 "Drone Age".
it_zsu_23_4: Some 6,500 Shilkas were built in the Soviet Union between 1964 and 1982; the ZSU-23-4V was an early update with better crew conditions and reliability, and Hungary received about 50 in 1969, retiring them in the 1990s. In capable hands its rapid, accurate fire makes it a serious threat to aircraft, helicopters, ATGMs and drones at short to medium range. It is no match for tanks, and its armour is weak. The Hungarian version came in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila" in the Italian ground tree.
it_zsu_57_2: Built on a heavily modified T-54 chassis, the ZSU-57-2 mounts twin 57 mm anti-aircraft guns and was taken up by Hungary, Bulgaria and Romania alongside the Soviet Army. Its high-velocity cannons and choice of shells handle both air and ground targets, though in practice they are a bigger menace to vehicles than to aircraft, given limited sustained fire and accuracy. The T-54 running gear gives it good mobility, but the armour is very light and the vehicle too large to hide, so it should stay close to allies when pushing. It joined the Hungarian subtree of the Italian tree in the "Sons of Attila" update.
itp_m1: The ITP, Russian shorthand for "heavy cannon fighter", was a Polikarpov prototype that looks like a blend of the MiG-3 and I-185. Like the Yak-9T, it fires a 37 mm cannon through the propeller hub, supported by two 20 mm ShVAK cannons with plenty of ammunition. Good flight performance lets an accurate pilot destroy targets quickly, and that firepower makes it equally useful against fighters, bombers and tanks in air or mixed battles, a versatility few Soviet aircraft match. It was a Battle Pass Season II "Steel Centurion" reward in the "Hot Tracks" update.
j1n1_mod11_early: Begun in 1938 as a long-range bomber escort for the Japanese Navy, the J1N1 reached trials only in 1941, by which time the A6M had shown it could do the job; poor agility and unreliable remote turrets kept it from the fighter role, but its range led to reconnaissance and later Gekkō night-fighter versions, and it was the basis for the J5N Tenrai. In the game, leading-edge slats and automatic flaps ease its twin-engine handling, and it carries a 20 mm cannon plus four 7.7 mm guns in two wide-arc remote turrets. Hunting bombers first, then using altitude for boom-and-zoom attacks, gets the most from it. It was added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
j2m2: Mitsubishi's J2M Raiden, designed by Jiro Horikoshi's team after a 1939 Navy request for a base-defence interceptor against high-flying bombers, was dogged by engine vibration and landing gear problems, so instead of replacing the A6M it served as a stopgap until the N1K-J Shiden arrived. The J2M2 Model 11 was the first production version. In the game its two machine guns are secondary to its two hard-hitting cannons, and an excellent climb rate and high diving speed make it a boom-and-zoom aircraft. Handling is average at low to medium speed and stiffens badly in fast dives. It was introduced in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
j2m3: The J2M3 Model 21, the most numerous Raiden, swapped the nose machine guns for a second pair of 20 mm cannons in the wings and moved to belt feeds for greater ammunition capacity. With four 20 mm cannons, two Type 99 Model 1s and two Model 2s, a single firing pass is often enough to bring a target down. The engine is unchanged, so it climbs as well as the J2M2, but it meets faster opponents that can keep up with it. It was introduced in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
j2m4_kai: The J2M4 Model 32 was a high-altitude Raiden prototype with a turbocharged Mitsubishi Kasei 23C engine that stretched the nose; only two were built, as turbocharger trouble, poor weight balance and longer take-off and landing runs ended the project. Its 1,854 hp engine and turbocharger give it a clear edge over earlier Raidens at altitude, much like the later J2M5. It arrived as a Golden Eagle premium in Update 1.47 "Big Guns", left sale after the 9th Anniversary Sale, and has since returned briefly during the 2022 "Day of Japan" and 2023 "National Foundation Day in Japan" events.
j2m5: The J2M5 Model 33 was a high-altitude Raiden powered by the Mitsubishi Kasei 26a with a mechanically driven supercharger, trading range for speed up high; unlike the J2M4 it entered limited production and reached several units. In the game its 1,854 hp engine lifts performance above earlier Raidens while the weight distribution stays the same as the J2M2/3. It still climbs superbly and pairs the J2M3's four-cannon firepower with performance for its tier closer to that of the J2M2. It was introduced in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
j2m5_30mm: This J2M5 prototype exchanged the Raiden's four 20 mm cannons for two 30 mm Type 5 cannons, but shortages of materials and labour, plus constant bombing, kept it out of production. It flies exactly like the standard J2M5, so the difference lies in the guns: each 30 mm hit is devastating, but ammunition is very limited, so short, well-aimed bursts are essential. It was introduced in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
j5n1: Nakajima developed the J5N1 Tenrai from the J1N1 to meet a 1943 Navy call for a fast, heavily armed high-altitude fighter to counter bombers such as the B-24 and B-29; six prototypes were built, but it never reached its speed target despite several engine combinations and was weighed down by the Navy's long list of demands. In the game it is a capable high-altitude twin with heavy firepower and decent agility for its size. It should stay above the fight, diving on aircraft below and catching bombers before they reach their targets. It was introduced in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
j6b: The J6B was the last biplane fighter designed in Sweden, built by ASJA from 1933 to 1935 on a Svenska Aero design; it flew as a fighter until 1938, then as a trainer, and two went to Finland during the Winter War, serving there as trainers until 1945. In the game it is slow for a starter aircraft, but it turns superbly and climbs well, and its two fast-firing 8 mm guns make it lethal in skilled hands while staying forgiving for beginners. Several belt options let it fight both aircraft and ground targets in air realistic battles. It was added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
j6k1: Kawanishi's J6K1 Jinpū grew out of the abandoned J3K once the Nakajima Homare engine became available; the Navy inspected a wooden mock-up in 1944 but chose the N1K2-J Shiden Kai, and a later revival lost out to the A7M3-J. In the game it handles very well at medium speeds and carries six 20 mm wing cannons and two 13.2 mm guns, with enough ammunition for long or awkward-angle shots; HE-heavy belts shred fighters and bombers, while armoured-target belts and two bomb loads cover ground attack. Despite its size it turns competitively, and its flaps are a key dogfighting aid to be used with care. It was the main air reward of the 2019 Operation F.R.O.S.T. event in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
j7w1: Masayoshi Tsuruno's J7W1 Shinden placed the wings and pusher engine at the rear with a canard at the nose, freeing space up front for guns; conceived as a 400-knot fighter, it was refocused as a high-altitude interceptor against B-24 and B-29 raids, but only two prototypes were completed before the surrender. In the game it is a bomber killer with outstanding performance at altitude, very heavy armament and a decent climb. Twice the weight of a loaded A6M yet much faster, it holds energy well and suits boom-and-zoom, while the canard layout gives quick pitch changes and a strong roll rate at some cost to stability. It was introduced in Update 1.43.
j8m1: The Ki-200 Shūsui began as a licence copy of the Me 163 Komet, but with no complete example reaching Japan, engineers had to reconstruct both airframe and rocket motor from a manual and scant documents; Mitsubishi built it for both the Navy (J8M) and Army (Ki-200), keeping the German layout. It plays like the Me 163 B: fuel is scarce, so it climbs immediately, throttles back and dives on targets below. Its 30 mm cannons can kill with a single hit but carry little ammunition, and keeping altitude lets it glide home once the fuel is gone. It has been in the game since the start of open beta, before Update 1.27.
j9_early: The J9 was Sweden's designation for Seversky's P-35A, which the USAAC passed over in favour of a Curtiss design; Sweden ordered 120 in total, but only the first 60 arrived before the rest were diverted to the Pacific, where they suffered heavy losses. In the game it resembles early Italian monoplane fighters and carries four machine guns, two of them hard-hitting 13.2 mm with HEF rounds. It is somewhat slow for its tier but turns tightly and climbs decently, so it suits dogfighting after entering from above with energy in hand. It was a reward for the 2023 Winter Extreme event in the "Air Superiority" update.
j_10a: Chengdu's J-10A traces back to the canard J-9-VI studies of the 1960s and 1970s, revived by Song Wencong in 1982 as Project No. 10; packed with new components, including China's first digital fly-by-wire, it first flew in March 1998 and was formally presented in 2006 as the PLAAF's new multirole fighter. In the game it filled a long gap in the Chinese tree as a true all-rounder, with beyond-visual-range missiles comparable to the Su-27's and guided air-to-ground weapons previously limited to the JH-7A. Excellent agility and a large payload for its size make it a formidable opponent. It was added in the "Dance of Dragons" update.
j_10c: The J-10C is Chengdu's heavily upgraded J-10, first flown in December 2013 and in PLAAF service from 2018, with an AESA radar and a more powerful, economical AL-31FN Series 3 engine, though some later aircraft use Chinese engines; the export J-10CE serves with Pakistan, and the type first saw combat in the 2025 Indo-Pakistani conflict. In the game the new engine markedly improves thrust-to-weight, and the AESA radar supports confident long-range shots with PL-12 active radar missiles, backed by all-aspect PL-8B missiles for close fights. Its missiles have shorter launch ranges than some rivals' and the cannon is awkward to aim. It was introduced in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
j_11: China's first Flankers were Su-27SKs ordered from the Soviet Union in 1990–91, after PLAAF officers visiting Kubinka passed over the MiG-29 in favour of the Su-27; a 1996 deal for 200 locally assembled jets followed, and Chinese refinement of the design paved the way for the J-11B. In the game it performs almost identically to the Soviet Su-27, despite being 570 kg heavier, combining refined aerodynamics, powerful engines, a large air-to-air load and capable radar and IRST. Its size and dated electronics can be liabilities. It came in the "Air Superiority" update.
j_11a: The J-11A is the Shenyang-assembled Su-27SK, built from 1998 under the 1996 licence deal; to give it active radar missiles, Belarus's 558th Aircraft Repair Plant later rewired its fire control so that RVV-AE missiles registered as R-27s, and some Guangdong-based aircraft gained domestic UV missile warners for South China Sea patrols. In the game that brings active radar homing missiles and slightly better situational awareness than the J-11. The Russian-era avionics remain a weakness, but handling and overall combat ability match or edge the original. It was introduced in the "Seek & Destroy" update.
j_11b: Shenyang used digitised Su-27 blueprints from its J-11A production to create the J-11B, with domestic avionics, composite materials and provision for new engines; work began in 1998, it flew in December 2003 and joined the PLAAF in 2006, notably the Flanker-experienced 1st Division at Anshan. In the game compact, efficient domestic avionics, particularly the new radar, replace the bulky Soviet-era equipment, while weight savings and more powerful Chinese engines make it more agile than earlier Flankers. It carries fewer missiles than some rival interceptors but still a large payload. It was introduced in the "Hornet's Sting" update.
j_15t: After talks to buy Su-33s stalled, China developed the J-15 carrier fighter, reportedly from the Su-33 prototype T-10K-03 obtained from Ukraine; it first operated from a carrier in 2012. The J-15T, unveiled in 2021 after land-based catapult trials from 2016, can launch from both ski-jump and catapult carriers and has much-upgraded avionics. In the game it keeps the J-11B's agility and large load of air-to-air and air-to-ground missiles, adds a new radar and PL-12A missiles, and for mixed battles can carry 500 kg IR-guided bombs and KD-88 missiles. Its size and weight leave it behind lighter Western fighters in performance. It was introduced in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
j_16: Shenyang's J-16 is a two-seat multirole strike fighter derived, via the J-11BS, from the Su-27UB; it first flew in October 2011 and reached the PLAAF in 2014, and its AESA radar can track distant aircraft and guide weapons onto several surface targets at once. In the game it is fast and climbs well but is less agile than lighter fighters, so long dogfights are risky. PL-12A and PL-8B missiles handle air threats, while LD-10 and YJ-91A anti-radiation missiles, YJ-83K anti-ship missiles, KD-88A missiles, many guided bombs and a targeting pod make it a serious danger to armour in mixed battles. It was introduced in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
j_22m1a: The J-22 began with a 1971 Romanian–Yugoslav agreement to build a simple, rugged subsonic attack jet from local parts; both prototypes flew on 31 October 1974, 165 were built by 1992, and the type fought in the Yugoslav Wars and still serves Serbia. The J-22M1A is Serbia's latest upgrade, adding a glass cockpit, a new RWR and modern weapons, with at least four in service in the 2020s. In the game it brings strong anti-tank armament, a ballistic computer and good handling, but it has no countermeasures, no air-to-air missiles unlike the IAR-93B, and modest speed for a jet. Created through the Revenue Share programme, it joined the USSR tree in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
j_7_mk2: Chengdu's J-7 was a MiG-21F-13 reverse-engineered without full documentation amid strained Sino-Soviet ties, with around 250 problems fixed along the way, including the fuel system, ejection seat and canopy. The J-7II was a cheap, simple point-defence day fighter with two 30 mm cannons and two PL-2 missiles, meant to overwhelm Western jets through numbers. In the game it is very fast in a straight line, nearing Mach 2, but hard turns bleed energy and regaining speed below 700 km/h usually needs a dive, so being low and slow is dangerous. The PL-2 is awkward to use, HF-4 rockets work against bombers, and only 120 cannon rounds demand trigger discipline. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
j_7d: The J-7D, or J-7IIIA, upgraded the J-7C, itself developed from MiG-21MFs obtained from Egypt and fitted with Chinese avionics and a HUD; it was meant to cover the PLAAF's interceptor needs while the J-8 programme lagged, but the J-8II and the arrival of the Su-27SK and J-11A left room for only a few orders using existing airframes. In the game it performs much like late MiG-21s, with a better engine and more fuel. It lacks missiles for head-on interceptions and heavy rockets such as the S-24, but IR missiles and a range of Chinese ground-attack weapons keep it capable. It was introduced in the "Apex Predators" update.
j_7e: The J-7E is a heavily reworked Chinese MiG-21 with a double-delta wing, developed in the late 1980s both to replace the PLAAF's J-6s and to earn export income towards the J-10 programme; though dated, it remains cheap to run and doubles as a lead-in trainer. In the game it takes a different route from Soviet Fishbed upgrades: a stronger engine and extra fuel combine with the slatted double-delta wing to give manoeuvrability, especially at low speed, that no Soviet MiG-21 can match. PL-5B missiles and a large countermeasure supply let a skilled pilot dominate close fights even against stronger aircraft. It was introduced in the "Red Skies" update.
j_8b: The J-8B, the first series of the J-8II, reworked the nose-intake J-8I to face the MiG-23 and later aircraft such as the F-16A, entering production in the early 1990s with modest avionics and serving about a decade before upgrades. In the game it was the first Chinese jet with search radar and semi-active radar missiles. Over 20 m long yet lighter than an F-4 or MiG-23, it has twin WP-13 engines and clean aerodynamics for strong acceleration and climb, and can turn when it must. The Type 208A radar lacks a boresight mode and only four missiles fit, so dedicated BVR fighters such as the F-4J are best avoided. It came in the "Wind of Change" update.
j_8f: The J-8F was the last combat model of the J-8 line, built by Shenyang in the mid-2000s from leftover J-8II airframes or converted J-8Ds; its radar descended from the abandoned J-8C project, and with access to active radar missiles it remained a PLAAF mainstay until replacements began arriving in 2022. In the game it is the first Chinese jet with a pulse-Doppler radar, carrying PL-8 and PL-12 missiles on every wing pylon. More powerful engines, a new RWR and the J-8II's differential elevators for faster roll round out the upgrade. It was introduced in the "La Royale" update.
jaguar_a: The Jaguar came from a 1960s Anglo-French effort, run through the SEPECAT consortium, to build a cheap trainer and light attack aircraft, with Rolls-Royce and Turbomeca sharing the Adour engine and Breguet and BAC the airframe; it grew into a widely exported strike aircraft. The Jaguar A was the French Air Force's single-seat all-weather attack version, with 160 built. Fully loaded it is heavy and sluggish, so in air battles it often flies light as a nimble support fighter with plenty of countermeasures and R.550 Magic 1 missiles. Mixed battles suit it best, where BGL laser-guided bombs and AS-30L missiles lead a broad arsenal. It came in the "Raining Fire" update.
jaguar_e: The Jaguar E was the French Air Force's two-seat training version of the Anglo-French SEPECAT Jaguar, with two prototypes and 40 production aircraft built. It shares the Jaguar A's toolkit: R.550 Magic 1 missiles and ample countermeasures for a light support-fighter role in air battles, and BGL laser-guided bombs and AS-30L missiles for strike work in mixed battles. Its heavier airframe and take-off weight, however, leave it handling and performing worse than the single-seater, especially when loaded. It was the reward for the 2022 Project "Overpowered" event during the "Drone Age" update.
jaguar_gr1: Conceived in the Anglo-French Jaguar programme as a trainer and light attacker, the Jaguar matured into a supersonic precision strike aircraft, entering RAF service in 1974, seeing combat in the Gulf, Iraq and Kargil wars among its various users, and leaving the RAF in 2007 in favour of the Typhoon. In the game the GR.1 has afterburning engines, a very heavy ground-attack load and a ballistic computer, but it is poorly suited to air combat and carries no countermeasures. That calls for careful, deliberate strike runs, where its payload makes it well worth flying. It was introduced in the "Raining Fire" update.
jaguar_gr1a: From 1983 the RAF upgraded its Jaguars to GR.1A standard, adding the Ferranti FIN 1064 inertial navigation and computer, stronger Adour Mk.104 engines, provision for countermeasure and targeting pods, and better IFF and radios; the type flew close support, interdiction and reconnaissance in the 1991 Gulf War. In the game it flies much like the GR.1 but is far more capable: Mk.13 guided bombs with a TIALD targeting pod are the headline addition, and countermeasures greatly improve its survival, making it dangerous both to ground targets and to aircraft. It was introduced in the "Ground Breaking" update.
jaguar_is: The Jaguar IS is India's export version of the Anglo-French Jaguar, in continuous service with Indian squadrons since 1981. Its range of hardpoint weapons is modest next to its contemporaries, yet it can still carry up to 8,000 lb of bombs. Like the GR.1A it has over-wing missile rails, so it keeps its air-to-air missiles whatever ground ordnance it carries, and these are a pair of very effective R550 Magic 2s. It was a reward for the 2024 Sword of Justice event in the "Air Superiority" update.
javelin_fmk9: Gloster's Javelin answered a late-1940s Air Ministry call for a two-seat, radar-equipped jet night fighter able to climb quickly and intercept Soviet jet bombers at up to 40,000 ft, beating a de Havilland rival to enter service as an all-weather fighter in the 1950s. In the game it continues the Meteor's approach and anticipates later British interceptors such as the Lightning and Tornado F.3: plenty of engine power, but less agility than its opponents. What it lacks in handling it makes up in firepower, with 30 mm ADEN cannons, Firestreak missiles and a strong radar for its tier. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
jf_17: The JF-17 was born from a 1995 Sino-Pakistani agreement after the earlier Sabre II upgrade of the F-7 collapsed under US sanctions; the first prototype flew in September 2003, deliveries to Pakistan began in 2007, and it also serves Myanmar and Nigeria. In the game it combines short-ranged but potent active radar missiles, exceptional agility, a dependable radar and a decent RWR. On the downside, top speed is low, energy drains fast in turns, the cannon is awkwardly placed, and its flares can run out early. It was introduced in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
jh_7: China began the JH-7 Flying Leopard in the 1970s to replace H-5 bombers and Q-5 attack aircraft, but inexperience, not least with engines, meant it relied on imported Rolls-Royce Spey Mk.202 turbofans and did not fly until late 1988; only twelve reached the air force from 1994, by then outdated and unreliable. In the game this early model has no guided weapons or targeting pod, so it relies on fine flight performance and a ballistic computer to deliver unguided bombs and rockets. It was introduced in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
jh_7a: Designed by Nanchang and later improved by Xi'an, the JH-7 two-seat strike fighter was meant to bring Chinese naval aviation closer to aircraft such as the F-15E and Su-34, with the JH-7A becoming the production model that modernised the naval air arm. In the game it is a dedicated striker: precision ground weapons and a powerful targeting pod make it shine in mixed battles, and its strong radar with all-aspect PL-8 and PL-5C missiles gives useful self-defence. In pure air modes it struggles against dedicated fighters. It is a big leap over the Q-5 family before it in the tree, and arrived in Update 2.31 "Kings of Battle".
jh_7a2: Unveiled by China's defence ministry in October 2021, the JH-7A2 upgrades the JH-7A with a wider range of precision weapons, including TV-guided KD-88A and CM-102 anti-radiation missiles, plus PL-12 active radar missiles for self-defence. In the game the PL-12s are the key change, letting it engage aircraft at medium range without holding a radar lock, and it also gains IR-guided bombs. Good low-level speed and a sturdy airframe help it survive; it is a serious threat to tanks in mixed battles and can hit bases while fending off fighters in air battles. It was introduced in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
jh_7a_prototype: The JH-7A Flying Leopard II reached units in numbers from 2004 with a JL-10A pulse-Doppler radar, digital weapons control, guided bombs and missiles and a targeting pod, and some 240 now form the core of Chinese strike aviation. This prototype differs from the researchable JH-7A only in its unique camouflage. Laser-guided bombs, fire-and-forget Kh-29T missiles and a thermal targeting pod make it dangerous in mixed battles. It is outflown by rival aircraft, but plentiful countermeasures and PL-8 and PL-5 missiles let it hold its own in the air. It was introduced in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
jp_btr_3e1: Ukraine's Morozov bureau developed the BTR-3 from the BTR-80 after independence, first showing it in 2001; the export BTR-3E1, armed with the BM-3M Shturm-M module, was ordered by Thailand in 2007, delivered between 2010 and 2016 and, alongside the Oplot-T, took part in the 2025–26 conflict with Cambodia. Despite looking like the BTR-82AT, it shares little but mobility: it carries a 30 mm cannon with APDS for light targets, a 30 mm grenade launcher and Barrier missiles with tandem warheads for long-range tank kills. It has no APFSDS belt and only light armour. It was introduced in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
jp_halftrack_m16: Japan received American M16 halftracks as post-war surplus, operating them through the National Safety Forces and the JGSDF until they were retired as obsolete in 1974. In the game it is identical to the American M16 MGMC: four 12.7 mm M2HB machine guns on one mount bring down aircraft through sheer volume of fire, helped by incendiary rounds in the belts. Armour offers little protection, though the crew layout means it often survives being hit. It was introduced in the "Direct Hit" update.
jp_harimau: Jointly developed by Indonesia and Turkey from 2015 to replace Indonesia's ageing AMX-13s, the Harimau, also called the Kaplan MMWT, pairs an FNSS hull with Belgium's Cockerill 3105 turret; 18 are in service, and Pindad plans to build over 400 more locally. Its 105 mm gun fires DM63 APFSDS that can defeat the front of some main battle tanks, and gunner and commander both get third-generation thermal sights. Protection is thin enough that 20 mm cannons can hurt it from some angles, so it relies on mobility: around 70 km/h forward and about half that in reverse. It was introduced in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
jp_hiro_sha: The Ro-Go Exp. reworked the Ro-Go heavy tank hull to carry a French-designed 120 mm Schneider-Canet Model 1898 gun, turning spare hulls into powerful but fragile self-propelled guns. In the game the gun outclasses most of what it meets, but the heavy hull is slow and sluggish, and the open top and thin armour leave it badly exposed. It works best as a long-range sniper picking off targets from a safe position. It was introduced in the "Ixwa Strike" update.
jp_icv_ifv_prototype: Mitsubishi's infantry combat variant of the Common Tactical Wheeled Vehicle, built on the Type 16 MCV platform, carries an unmanned turret with a 30 mm Bushmaster and was trialled in 2023–24 before procurement as the Type 24 ICV began in FY2024; it is probably assigned to rapid deployment regiments alongside their MCVs. In the game it plays much like other Bushmaster-armed scouts such as the VBCI-2. Because the turret is crewless, it can rise over cover and fire with only the gun and ammunition exposed, keeping the crew out of harm's way. It was introduced in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
jp_icv_prototype: Mitsubishi's reconnaissance version of the Common Tactical Wheeled Vehicle, based on the Type 16 MCV, adds a 30 mm Bushmaster, a surveillance camera and a satellite antenna; tested in 2023–24, it is set for procurement as the Type 25 RCV from FY2025 to modernise JGSDF reconnaissance. In the game it offers the same aggressive scouting as other 30 mm Bushmaster vehicles like the VBCI-2. Its standout feature is a commander's mast that extends about 2 m, letting it spot targets, and even direct the gun, while the hull stays hidden behind cover. It was introduced in the "Dance of Dragons" update.
jp_leopard_2ri: IBD Deisenroth's Leopard 2 upgrade, which boosts a 2A4's protection, firepower and awareness without a new turret, found a buyer in Indonesia in 2013; 61 of its 103 tanks became Leopard 2RIs with AMAP armour modules, an electric turret drive and updated fire control, delivered in 2016–17 and never used in combat. In the game it is a balanced tank whose gun defeats any opponent frontally, with fire control that works at any range, day or night, and enough mobility to lead pushes and take points. Its armour is tuned against chemical rounds, so kinetic shells usually get through; a large crew and roomy interior help it survive a first hit, but not always to fight back. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry" in the Japanese tree.
jp_m163_vulcan: Thailand ordered 24 American M163 Vulcan air-defence vehicles in 1981 as part of a wider purchase of US surplus equipment, but as the system was outdated for its intended role it served mainly in fire-support and anti-infantry duties until an upgrade by Israel's IMI in 2015. In the game it is identical to the American M163: its 20 mm Vulcan has a very high rate of fire but limited reach compared with bigger systems, so it must work close to the front to cover allies, where overextending is a constant risk. It arrived in the "Tusk Force" update as part of the Japanese ground tree.
jp_m19: Like the M16, the M19A1 came to Japan as American surplus after WWII to help found the Self-Defence Forces, serving with the JASDF and JGSDF until it was retired as obsolete in 1979. It is identical to the American version, with twin 40 mm guns in a large open turret on the M24 Chaffee chassis. The guns penetrate well enough for flanking ground targets. Against aircraft the lower fire rate makes hits harder to land than with earlier Japanese anti-aircraft vehicles, but the fast, heavy shells can wreck a plane with a single hit. It was introduced in the "Direct Hit" update.
jp_m24_chaffee: The US supplied M24s to Japan alongside M4A3 (76) W Shermans when the Korean War spurred the rebuilding of Japan's forces; crews liked it, though its short 75 mm was already outmatched by tanks like the T-34-85. In the game it is identical to the American M24, a nimble light tank with Sherman-level firepower against the low-rank opposition it meets. The effective M61 APCBC, smoke grenades, a .50 cal machine gun, a forgiving reverse and scouting make it versatile enough to outflank and beat most opponents. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_m36b2_jgsdf: A single M36 was given to the JGSDF purely for research, aiding the domestic tank programme that produced the Type 61. In the game it improves on the standard M36 GMC with a new muzzle brake and bore evacuator, the better-penetrating M82A1 round, a hull machine gun and 6 mm of roof armour. Its most valuable asset is HEAT-FS ammunition, which destroys most targets with ease. It was introduced in the "Danger Zone" update.
jp_m41_walker_bulldog: Supplied under Japan's second defence build-up plan, the M41A1 replaced the outdated M24 while the domestic Type 61 took over from the M4A3 (76) W. In the game it matches the American M41 and returns to the M24's shoot-and-scoot style: a fast, agile flanker with a respectable 76 mm gun. With only solid shot available, knowing opponents' internal layouts is essential to make hits count. Nearly everything it meets, anti-aircraft vehicles included, can penetrate its armour, so cover and awareness are vital. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_m42_duster: Japan bought a small number of M42s in the 1960s to replace the M19, keeping purchases low because of the cost of developing the Type 87, and kept them until 1994 even though the Type 87 was adopted in 1987. Identical to the American M42, it is a middling anti-aircraft vehicle: the twin 40 mm Bofors fire slowly, making quick hits hard, and the exposed crew can be strafed to pieces by any aircraft. Its speed, though, lets it relocate quickly. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_m44: Built on a reversed M41 chassis and standardised in 1954, too late for Korea, the American M44 howitzer went to allies including Japan, which accepted 10 M44A1s for its 7th Artillery Regiment until the Type 75 replaced them in 1986. In the game it is mobile and lightly armoured, firing the powerful M107 155 mm HE shell, though the short barrel's low velocity and heavy drop demand careful aim. The open casemate and narrow traverse leave its six crew exposed, but their number aids survival, and a .50 cal machine gun offers some answer to aircraft and light vehicles. It was introduced in the "Storm Warning" update.
jp_m47_patton_II: The JGSDF wanted to trial the M47, but with German orders delaying delivery Japan began its own ST-A designs; when an M47 finally arrived partway through, the comparison convinced Japan to continue with its domestic tank, the future Type 61. In the game it is identical to the American M47 and offers sturdier armour than Japanese crews are used to, though the APDS and HEAT rounds common at its level largely negate it. It is best played like other Japanese mediums, relying on its strong gun while staying cautious, much like the ST-As and Type 61 before it. It was introduced in the "Red Skies" update.
jp_m4a3e8_76w_sherman: Shermans of this type reached Japan with M24s when the Korean War prompted its rearmament, after the US State Department blocked the M26s originally intended. Their 76 mm guns were weaker than 90 mm alternatives and the tanks were large for Japanese crews, so the domestic Type 61 replaced them by the end of the decade. In the game it is identical to the American M4A3 (76) W HVSS, with good firepower and mobility but rather weak armour, making a well-rounded tank when played sensibly. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_m60a3_tts: Thailand bought 125 retired US Army M60A3 TTS tanks between 1985 and 1990; they fought Myanmar's army in a 2001 border clash and remain in service despite the later arrival of the Oplot-T and VT-4. In the game it performs exactly like the Taiwanese M60A3, with thermal sights, a two-plane stabiliser, good gun handling and a wide choice of ammunition. On the other hand it is large, only averagely mobile and lacks the ERA of the American version, leaving protection inadequate. It was added to the Japanese ground tree in the "Tusk Force" update.
jp_navy_120mm_spg: An obscure one-off found by US Marines at the Yokosuka Naval Arsenal, the Chi-Ha LG was built by the Imperial Navy on a gutted, reinforced Chi-Ha hull carrying a 12 cm/45 10th Year naval gun, a weapon normally found on cruisers, carriers and coastal batteries. It is effectively a mobile gun emplacement: the crew is completely exposed and the heavy gun saps mobility, so firing from a distance and ducking back into cover is the only real tactic. The 120 mm SAPCBC-HE shell, at 825 m/s with about 100 mm of penetration at 300 m, hits very hard, but recoil throws the aim off after each shot. It came in the "Raining Fire" update.
jp_oplot_t: Ukraine's T-84 Oplot, built by KMDB since 1995, developed the T-80UD with a welded turret, Nizh ERA and a revised drivetrain that greatly improves reversing; Thailand ordered 49 of its Oplot-T version in 2011, with local radios and air conditioning, and deliveries finished in March 2018 after long delays. In the game its 32 km/h reverse is unusual for an Eastern-bloc design and makes repositioning easy, while layers of ERA and NERA plus an APS guard its three crew. The gun is underwhelming and depresses poorly, and gaps such as the one between side skirts and hull can be exploited. It arrived in the Japanese tree with the "Tusk Force" update.
