jp_pzkpfw_VI_ausf_e_tiger: Prompted by ambassador General Hiroshi Ōshima, who had seen Tigers on the Eastern Front, Japan bought Tiger chassis 250455 in 1943 and planned to ship it home by submarine; Allied control of the seas prevented delivery, so it was lent back to Germany and served with the 101st SS Heavy Panzer Battalion. In the game it pairs a late Tiger E turret with a mid-production H1 hull and ammunition, without the E's thicker turret roof. Its 100 mm front, best angled, and 88 mm KwK36 suit both sniping and brawling, though S-mine launchers on the front hull corners restrict gun depression over them. It was a pre-order pack at the Japanese tree's launch in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai", withdrawn after the 2019 summer sale.
jp_st_a1: Japan's first post-war tank design, the ST-A1 was the opening prototype on the road to the Type 61, drawing heavily on the M46 Patton and carrying a 90 mm M3 gun with HEAT-FS for Soviet armour. Its armour is light and its crew, modules and ammunition are tightly packed, so a single hit often finishes it. A low profile and strong gun make long-range shots from cover its best tactic, and while flanking is possible it is not especially quick; an excellent reverse speed helps it duck back behind cover. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_st_a2: The second prototype towards the Type 61, the ST-A2 looked increasingly like the finished tank, differing from the ST-A1 mainly in hull design while keeping the same engine, weight and gun. In the game it is a sidegrade to the ST-A1 rather than an upgrade: a sniper first, with little aptitude for other roles, and the two can largely be treated as one tank apart from small quality-of-life differences. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_st_a3: The ST-A3 was the third and last completed Type 61 prototype, from the second development phase that, with the ST-A4, cured the earlier transmission problems; the ST-A4 was finished first and, easier to build and with a larger cupola, became the basis for the Type 61, leaving the autoloaded ST-A3 behind. In the game it is essentially a Type 61 with an autoloader cycling every 6 seconds through an 11-round first stage, about a second quicker than the production tank and unaffected by crew losses. Its smaller cupola is harder to hit, and the shielded machine gun elevates higher for anti-air use. It was introduced in the "Hot Tracks" update.
jp_st_b1: Developed soon after the Type 61 entered service, the STB-2 was a prototype of the Type 74, meant to close the gap with the T-62, M60 and Leopard 1 by adopting the L7-type 105 mm rifled gun. In the game it carries more armour than the Leopard 1 or early AMX-30 with similar mobility, yet it still suits cautious hit-and-run play rather than front-line fighting. Its hydropneumatic suspension improves gun depression and can aid survival, and a laser rangefinder, unusual at its rank, gives it an edge at long range, whether lobbing low-velocity HESH accurately or ranging APDS shots quickly. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_stingray: Cadillac Gage began the Stingray in 1983 as a private export venture; after trials in Thailand from 1986 to replace the M41, the Royal Thai Army ordered 106 in 1989–90, becoming its only user, and used it in the 2013–14 border skirmishes with Cambodia. Identical to the American tree's Stingray, it is a classic light tank: quick and agile, with a 105 mm gun firing strong APFSDS, a two-plane stabiliser and a laser rangefinder for accurate long-range shots. The angled front can stop autocannon fire but should not be trusted, and the slow reverse makes escaping trouble difficult. It joined the Japanese tree in the "Tusk Force" update.
jp_sub_i_ii_20mm: One of several prototypes for the Type 73 armoured personnel carrier that replaced the smaller Type 60, the SUB-I-II was trialled with a 20 mm Rh202 cannon for self-defence and anti-aircraft use, an armament the production vehicle did not keep. In the game the cannon fires rapidly and can use an APDS belt, letting it shred suitable targets when positioned well. The amphibious hull, however, has no more than 20 mm of armour and is easily knocked out. It was introduced in the "Apex Predators" update.
jp_tkx_prot: The TKX-2-0005 was the third prototype of the Type 10, designed from 2002 to 2009 to replace the Type 74 and Type 90 with a tank light enough for most Japanese infrastructure while matching the Type 90's protection and adding modern C4I systems. In the game it shares the Type 90's strong firepower, with more compact armour of similar effectiveness and a less powerful engine to save weight. Its key advantage over the Type 90 is the Type 10 APFSDS round, which far outperforms JM33/DM33 and competes with other nations' best. Unlike the production Type 10, it can also fit a dozer blade once researched. It was introduced in the "Fire and Ice" update.
jp_type_03_chusam_fcs: The Type 03 Chū-SAM is Japan's home-grown replacement for the MIM-23 Hawk, developed from 1995 after its arms-export rules kept it out of the multinational MEADS programme; the main vehicles ride on heavy crane truck chassis, and the system cut a battery's crew from about 50 to around 20. This is the radar vehicle, whose phased-array antenna covers all directions out to 100 km, detecting up to 100 targets and tracking 12, with search, tracking and fire control in one unit. In the game it anchors Japan's longest-range mobile SAM; since the missiles rely on it, losing this vehicle disables the whole system. It was introduced in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
jp_type_03_chusam_launcher: These launcher vehicles belong to the Type 03 Chū-SAM, Japan's domestic successor to the MIM-23 Hawk, developed from 1995 on self-propelled heavy truck chassis after export rules kept Japan out of the MEADS programme. Each carries six vertically launched missiles that can pull up to 36 G, fly at around 1,120 m/s and engage targets out to about 80 km, using inertial mid-course guidance with radar updates. Without thrust vectoring, the missiles need room to turn after launch, giving a minimum range of roughly 3–4 km, but beyond that the system is extremely deadly. It was introduced in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact" as Japan's longest-range mobile SAM.
jp_type_10: The Type 10 is the production result of the TK-X programme, accepted in 2010 to supplement and replace the Type 74 and Type 90, with more emphasis on C4I, lower weight and modular armour. In the game, like the TKX, it is densely armoured but less powerfully engined than the heavier Type 90, and fires the excellent Type 10 APFSDS every 4 seconds. The quick reload suits close fights, while third-generation thermals, good zoom, a laser warning system and a rangefinder make it a fine sniper. Its weaknesses are a slow refill of the first-stage ammunition rack and armour that trails other top-tier tanks. It was introduced in the "Winged Lions" update.
jp_type_10_prototype: The TKX (P) is an early Type 10 prototype, a basic platform built to accept the modular armour kits central to the programme's goals of cutting weight, keeping protection and adding C4I systems. In the game it complements the Type 90 with third-generation thermals in place of first-generation and a smaller gun mantlet, at the cost of weaker turret sides and lower mobility. Lacking the Type 10's distinctive APFSDS, it combines Type 16-like handling and spotting traits with the Type 90's firepower. It was introduced in the "Sons of Attila" update.
jp_type_16: The Type 16 Maneuver Combat Vehicle is Japan's first wheeled assault gun, designed to strike from the flanks using good roads and easier terrain, and able to absorb some autocannon fire. In the game its high speed lets it cross the map quickly, while third-generation thermals and a laser rangefinder help it find and engage targets on the move, both on the flanks and at long range. A laser warning system gives it a chance to dodge long-range shots, and smoke grenades can hide it from helicopters. It was introduced in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
jp_type_16_mcv_prot: The third of four Type 16 prototypes, MCV No.3 (99-0292) differs from the production vehicle in its turret shape, gun mounting and chassis, and was tested by the JGSDF in 2014–15 before series production began in 2016. In play it follows the Type 16's formula: a fast wheeled hunter with third-generation thermals and a laser rangefinder for quick target acquisition, a laser warning system to react to incoming fire, and smoke to screen it from helicopters. It is at its best on flanks and at range. It came in the "Drone Age" update.
jp_type_16_mod: This is an early production Type 16 belonging to the 1st 16 MCV company of the 15th Rapid Deployment Regiment, 14th Brigade. It combines the ammunition and handling of the Type 16 (P) with the armour of the production Type 16. High wheeled speed, third-generation thermals and a laser rangefinder let it hunt on flanks and at long range, while a laser warning system and smoke grenades help it evade return fire and helicopters. It was sold as a premium pack from the "Sky Guardians" update.
jp_type_1_chi_he: The Chi-He refined the Chi-Ha Kai with welded instead of riveted armour, a little more protection, a stronger engine and a fifth crewman, yet weighed only 1.5 tonnes more; production began only in 1943 because the Navy had priority on materials, and all were held back for home defence. It still fell short of the M4 Sherman, and its hull went on to underpin the Type 3 Chi-Nu. In the game it keeps the Chi-Ha Kai's 47 mm Type 1 gun with better armour and slightly better mobility, making it enjoyable at low ranks. Good gun depression suits firing over hills, and a brisk reverse gets it out of trouble. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_1_chi_he_5th_regiment: This Chi-He represents the Imperial Japanese Army's 5th Tank Regiment, formed at Kurume in 1937 and sent to Manchuria, where inexperienced crews kept it in reserve during the Nomonhan fighting; it later trained and stood guard there before returning to defend Japan in 1945, never once seeing combat. In the game it plays exactly like the standard Chi-He, set apart only by a unique camouflage and three distinctive decals available on every camouflage. It was introduced in the "Regia Marina" update.
jp_type_2_ho_i: The Type 2 Ho-I was conceived to give the Chi-Ha's infantry-support role a 75 mm low-velocity gun able to crack bunkers its 57 mm could not; fitting the gun took until 1941, and the Chi-He hull was chosen for production. In the game it is essentially a Chi-He with a new turret and short 75 mm, playing like a smaller, faster Pz.IV E with a longer reload. Its HEAT shell penetrates around 90 mm, enough for most targets, and with average mobility it favours close fights, since the looping trajectory makes long shots demanding. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_2_ho_ni_2: The Ho-Ni II put the Type 91 10 cm howitzer on the Type 97 Chi-Ha chassis as mobile artillery, entering service in 1943; production estimates range from about 55 to 138. A battalion of Ho-Ni Is and IIs bound for the Philippines was lost when its convoy was sunk off Luzon, so most Ho-Ni IIs stayed in Japan for home defence. In the game the 105 mm howitzer's HE handles light vehicles, while HEAT gives an option against heavier ones, and it reloads more manageably than the Ho-Ro's 15 cm gun. The open fighting compartment and small front shield leave the crew exposed from the sides and rear and to overpressure. It was introduced in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
jp_type_2_ka_mi: The Navy's Special Ka-Mi was an amphibious light tank for landing operations, built on the Ha-Go with a watertight hull and add-on pontoons for rough seas. In the game it improves on the Ha-Go with the Type 1 37 mm gun and a coaxial machine gun, rare on Japanese wartime tanks. The pontoons are not modelled, but it still swims thanks to propellers on the hull, opening routes through water, and its shoulder-stabilised gun is easier to aim while bobbing on the waves. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_3_chi_nu: The Chi-Nu was a stopgap Sherman-fighter pending the Chi-To and Chi-Ri II: designers placed a new hexagonal turret on the Chi-He hull, carrying the Type 90 field gun adapted as the Type 3 75 mm tank gun. Approved in 1943, it entered production only in 1944 and was kept for defending the home islands. In the game it brings the balance of protection, firepower and mobility expected of a medium, and unlike earlier Japanese mediums its gun can kill contemporaries in one shot. It is flexible enough to join main assaults or flank in support. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_3_chi_nu_75cm_type_5: One of two plans to arm the Chi-Nu with the Type 5 75 mm gun of the Chi-To and Chi-Ri, the Chi-Nu II squeezed it into the standard Chi-Nu turret, while the other simply fitted a Chi-To turret. In the game it marries the Chi-Nu's hull, with only around 50 mm of armour, to the Chi-To's gun in a lower-profile package than the Chi-To. Its fragility makes it a long-range sniper rather than a close-quarters brawler. It was part of the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai", released once all rank III Japanese tanks were opened during closed beta.
jp_type_3_ho_ni_I: The Type 1 Ho-Ni I mounted a Type 90 75 mm field gun in an open casemate on the Type 97 chassis, providing fire support and anti-tank power for armoured divisions from 1942; many were lost against superior US forces on Luzon in 1945, and it was succeeded by the Ho-Ni II and Ho-Ni III. In the game its high-velocity gun penetrates most tanks it faces and can punch through the front of armour-reliant targets like the Char B1. Very thin armour and no turret leave it exposed to fire and flanking, so it is best used as a sniper or hull-down ambusher, exploiting its gun depression. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_3_ho_ni_III: Built from 1944 on obsolete Chi-Ha hulls to support the Chi-Nu, the Ho-Ni III carried the high-velocity Type 3 75 mm in a fully enclosed casemate; shortages and bombing limited production to 31, and most stayed in Japan without seeing combat. In the game it improves on the Ho-Ni I with more crew, a faster reload and protection for the gun crew, at the cost of top speed. The gun hits hard enough to snipe effectively, but the armour is weak, so it works best supporting allies from range and using smoke shells to create cover. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_3_ka_chi: The Navy's Special Ka-Chi scaled the Ka-Mi idea up onto the Chi-He, with plans for submarines to carry it close to islands for amphibious landings; with the Navy on the defensive from 1943, only 12–19 were built and all were kept for home defence. In the game it is essentially a giant amphibious Chi-He with the same turret, 47 mm gun, 50 mm maximum armour and engine. Its size spreads out the crew, including two extra engineers, and the pontoons act as spaced armour, making it much tougher than its numbers suggest, but the unchanged engine leaves it slow. It suits an improvised assault role, soaking fire while pushing. It was the 2021 Summer Landing event reward in the "Red Skies" update.
jp_type_4_chi_to: The Chi-To was Japan's answer to the Sherman's dominance over its 1930s infantry tanks, combining a new, larger hull with a long high-velocity 75 mm gun; delays in hull and gun development meant it was only ready for evaluation in 1945, with the Chi-Nu and Ho-Ni III built as stopgaps. In the game it sets the pattern for many later Japanese tanks: a very strong gun and decent mobility on a fragile body. Thin armour and a long reload make long-range duels its natural territory rather than close combat. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_4_chi_to_late: The Chi-To Late was the intended production version of the Chi-To, with a simplified, easier-to-build turret and slightly more steeply angled armour; shortages, bombing and the end of the war stopped production as with its predecessor. In the game the better armour angles make it a little more forgiving, bouncing shells somewhat more often, while the deadly high-velocity 75 mm is unchanged. It still belongs at sniping range rather than on the front line. It was introduced in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
jp_type_4_ho_ro: The Ho-Ro mounted a short 150 mm howitzer in an open superstructure on the Chi-Ha; around a dozen went to the Philippines with the 1st Self-Propelled Artillery Company in December 1944, where they knocked out several Shermans at 100–200 m in smoke and poor visibility, moving after each shot, until the last was destroyed in March 1945. In the game it is one of the most powerful howitzer vehicles despite its low rank, comparable to the KV-2: its HE shell destroys or cripples nearly anything, even top-tier tanks. The low shell velocity forces lobbed shots even at short range, and light armour and limited traverse balance it out. It has been in the game since Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_5_chi_ri: Shaped by Japanese reports on the German-Soviet war, the Chi-Ri was planned as a heavy medium tank favouring quality over numbers, with roughly the hull protection of a KV-1 and the firepower of a German long 75 mm; the drain of the wars in China and the Pacific saw resources shift to the more practical Chi-To. In the game its 75 mm reloads quickly and has a large first-stage ammunition rack. Even with its upgraded engine, the massive turret turns slowly, so the hull must help with aiming, and its sheer size makes it a big target. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_5_ho_ri_production: The Ho-Ri Production is a hypothetical production form of the Ho-Ri Prototype, with thicker armour and a longer gun. In the game it is much stronger than the prototype but faces stronger opponents and shares its basic drawbacks. The 120 mm front plate is effectively about 320 mm thick and the casemate offers 200–225 mm, so hull-down sniping with the −10° gun depression is the way to play, and it accelerates briskly to 40 km/h. To reach that depression the breech lifts part of the casemate roof, opening only a narrow gap that aircraft can rarely exploit and that does not expose the crew to overpressure. It was introduced in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
jp_type_5_ho_ri_prototype: The last of three designs for a tank destroyer armed with the new Type 5 105 mm anti-tank gun to face the heaviest US armour, the Ho-Ri used a Chi-Ri-derived hull and engine with a sloped front. In the game it resembles the Ferdinand: the hull front is effectively around 200 mm, though the lower plate hides driver, radio operator and transmission, while the casemate tops out at 150 mm and its cheeks at 125 mm. Hull-down sniping with −10° of depression, achieved by the breech lifting the roof, suits it best, and it accelerates quickly to 40 km/h. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.71 "New E.R.A." until the 2019 New Year sale, it returned for Golden Eagles in the May 2020 sale.
jp_type_5_na_to: The Na-To was a tank destroyer and testbed for the Type 5 75 mm gun, mounted on the Type 4 Chi-So armoured tracked carrier; the army ordered production, but barely any were finished before the war ended. In the game it is a classic gun-on-a-chassis design, vulnerable to almost everything because of its thin armour, yet devastating when it strikes first. Played as a rear-line sniper watching busy roads and choke points, it avoids becoming a priority target and can pull back to reload after each shot. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_60_atm: The Type 60 ATM was an armoured personnel carrier fitted with the Type 64 MAT, Japan's first-generation wire-guided anti-tank missile, which armed several vehicles. Armour is minimal, the missiles are slow, and while one is in flight control passes from the vehicle to the missile. The missile's upward arc, though, lets the vehicle sit behind solid cover and steer shots around or over obstacles with relative ease. It was introduced in Update 1.67 "Assault".
jp_type_60_sprg: Japan's first home-built combat vehicle after WWII, the Type 60 SPRG of the late 1950s was a small anti-tank vehicle carrying two 106 mm M40 recoilless rifles for ambushing tanks. It was also the first vehicle in War Thunder to use a recoilless gun as its main weapon. The pair of 106 mm guns is deadly at short range, but it struggles to contribute on maps with long sightlines. Its small size and fairly good mobility also make it an effective scout. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_61: Japan's first post-war service tank, the Type 61 grew out of the ST-A prototypes to replace the M4A3 (76) and M24, which were also too big for typical Japanese crews; built largely from American-origin components but Japanese in design, it entered service in 1961, already looked dated beside the M60, T-62 and Leopard 1, and served until 2000. In the game it resembles a cross between the M41 and the Patton family, with an M60-style turret and rangefinder cupola. It matches the M47 in firepower with its 90 mm gun and tall, fairly mobile build, but its armour is closer to an M41's. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_61_mod: The Type 61 (B) became the standard production version from 1966, bringing practical changes such as revised fuel stowage and relocated tools, and some received a Type 69 night sight and visible/IR searchlights for night units; the Type 61 family served until 2000. In the game it plays like the original Type 61: a tall, reasonably mobile tank with an M47-class 90 mm gun, an M60-style turret topped by a rangefinder cupola, and armour no better than an M41's. It was introduced in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
jp_type_74: The Type 74 (E) upgrades Japan's Type 74 with improved fire control that swaps Type 75 HESH for Type 91 HEAT-MP, keeps the thermal sleeve on the 105 mm L7A3 introduced with the (D), and can mount a dozer blade for digging in. It was the first Japanese MBT able to use APFSDS, and together with a laser rangefinder and hydropneumatic suspension that adjusts hull height and tilt, it makes a capable sniper. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai" as the Type 74 and became the Type 74 (E) in the "Direct Hit" update.
jp_type_74_c: One of the earliest production Type 74s, the (C) was Japan's second-generation MBT, intended to counter tanks like the T-62 and match the M60 and Leopard 1 while replacing the Type 61, though third-generation designs appeared only a few years later. It is distinguished from the later (E) by having no thermal sleeve on its 105 mm L7A3. In the game it lacks APFSDS, relying on APDS, HEAT and HESH, and has average mobility. The hydropneumatic suspension adjusts height and tilt to suit terrain, and a laser rangefinder and warning system make it an effective sniper. It was introduced in the "Direct Hit" update.
jp_type_74_f: The Type 74 (F) was the last minor update to the Type 74 line, adding hull mounting plates for the Type 92 mine roller. In the game it matches the Type 74 (E) apart from thin extra plates on the hull front and no dozer blade option. APFSDS, a laser rangefinder and hydropneumatic suspension that adjusts hull height and angle make it well suited to sniping. It was introduced in the "New Power" update.
jp_type_74_mod_g_kai: The Type 74 (G) came from a 1993 life-extension programme adding a passive infrared camera, side skirts, new electronics and a modified rear drive wheel to stop tracks coming off; trials went well, but cost meant only five tanks were upgraded, and the Type 74s were eventually replaced by the Type 16 MCV. In the game it differs from the (E) and (F) by swapping the IR searchlight for a thermal sight and adding side skirts for a marginal gain in protection. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.87 "Locked On" until the 2022 Winter sale, it returned briefly for Golden Eagles in the 2023 "National Foundation Day in Japan" event and permanently in the 2024 one.
jp_type_74_red_star: About 60 upgraded Type 74s received a new paint scheme as the (C) variant, and some ageing examples later went to the 1st Mechanized Battalion, a fictional hostile unit run by the JGSDF Training Evaluation Unit that dresses its vehicles to resemble Warsaw Pact equipment with red stars, drum fuel tanks, turret baggage and mud flaps. In the game it plays like the Type 74 (C), using APDS, HEAT and HESH without APFSDS, with average mobility, adjustable hydropneumatic suspension, a laser rangefinder and a warning system that suit sniping. A module removes the decorative rear tyres to improve gun depression over the back. It was introduced in the "Hornet's Sting" update.
jp_type_75: Developed from 1965 alongside the Type 74 tank and Type 73 APC, with shared components, the Type 75 replaced the M44 in Japanese service; MHI built the hull and JSW the 155 mm gun, and after trials of different barrel lengths and autoloaders it was finalised in December 1974 with a domestic L/30 barrel. Its standout feature is an automated feed that reloads in 10 seconds. The L/30 shoots slightly faster than the M109's L/24 but drops more than the M109A1's L/39 or Soviet 152 mm guns, which the domestic Type 75 HE shell offsets by trading filler for velocity. Armour stops only distant rifle fire and splinters. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
jp_type_75_mlrs: Komatsu's Type 75 multiple rocket launcher mounts 30 130 mm tubes, staggered in rows of 7, 8, 7 and 8, on a modified SUB-I Type 73 prototype hull, aiming 50° either side and up to 50° in elevation for barrages against fortifications, troops and vehicles. In the game it is far from a gimmick: each 43 kg rocket carries 6 kg of TNT equivalent and leaves at 700 m/s with fairly gentle drop. Unlike howitzers such as the Type 75 SPH or Type 99, it can fire its rockets one after another without reloading between shots, delivering fast, devastating volleys. It was introduced in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
jp_type_81_tansam: The Type 81 (C), or Tan-SAM Kai, is an upgrade of Japan's Type 81 short-range SAM begun in 1989 to bridge the gap between the Stinger and the Hawk, adopted as SAM-1C in 1995 with either an active radar seeker or an infrared and visible-light imaging seeker; this imaging version can operate alone, without the system's radar. In the game it is a larger, more potent big brother to the Type 93, with missiles pulling 35 G and reaching 955 m/s, plus a visual guidance mode that helps against helicopters carrying IR or electronic jammers. It still lacks radar, so despite a thermal camera, finding targets relies on situational awareness. It was introduced in the "Kings of Battle" update.
jp_type_81_tansam_fcs: Toshiba began the Type 81 Tan-SAM in 1966 to replace the M51 Skysweeper and M15A1, and it entered service in 1981, filling the gap between the Stinger and the Hawk; the improved Tan-SAM Kai, with radar-guided and imaging-seeker versions, was adopted in 1995 and built until 2005. This is the radar vehicle of the in-game three-vehicle battery, which also includes two launchers needing no extra research. Its large radar can, terrain permitting, detect aircraft long before they can fire, and losing it does not completely disable the system. The trade-off is a very large, conspicuous vehicle. It was introduced in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
jp_type_81_tansam_launcher: These launchers belong to the Tan-SAM Kai, the 1995 upgrade of Toshiba's Type 81 short-range missile system that has served Japan since 1981 between the Stinger and the Hawk. Two come with the radar vehicle and need no separate research. Unlike the imaging-seeker variant, they fire the Type 81C active radar missile, with much greater lock-on and launch range and immunity to flares, though targets get a launch warning. With two launchers, losing one is not critical, and losing the radar vehicle does not knock out the whole system either. They were introduced in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
jp_type_87: Japan's Type 87 follows the Gepard concept to replace the M15 and M42, moving from the Type 61 to the newer Type 74 hull during development; crews nicknamed it "Guntank" after the Mobile Suit Gundam mecha. In the game it uses the same twin 35 mm Oerlikon KDA guns and a similar layout to the Gepard, and its high fire rate, fast turret and radar make it effective against aircraft and especially helicopters like the AH-1G. It can also shred IFVs such as the BMP, Warrior and Bradley in seconds. Modern helicopters that stay at long range, like the Ka-50 or AH-64, are beyond its reach, leaving smoke and cover as its answer. It was introduced in Update 1.67 "Assault".
jp_type_87_rcv: Komatsu's 6x6 Type 87 reconnaissance vehicle entered JGSDF service in 1987, giving scouts more firepower and protection than jeeps and motorcycles once Japanese roads could support heavy wheeled vehicles. In the game it is fast and carries a rapid-firing 25 mm Oerlikon with a full APFSDS belt that penetrates most targets from the side or rear and some from the front, though damage after penetration is low. With no stabiliser and a bouncy suspension, its accuracy suffers. It was introduced in the "Direct Hit" update.
jp_type_87_rcv_prot: The prototype of the Type 87 RCV differs mainly in its turret, carrying a 20 mm cannon but also a costly stabiliser that was dropped from production vehicles. It keeps the production model's excellent mobility, but the smaller calibre means less penetration and damage. It is best used as intended, scouting from good vantage points and using the 20 mm only in self-defence or against soft targets such as other scouts. It was introduced in the "La Royale" update.
jp_type_89: Developed through the 1980s and adopted in 1989 to back up Japan's vulnerable APCs and work with the Type 90 tank, the Type 89 IFV proved so costly that only about 120 of the 300 ordered were built by 2014, mostly based in Hokkaido. In the game it pairs a 35 mm Oerlikon KDE with heavy Type 79 Jyu-MAT missiles. Hit-and-run tactics suit it, using speed and smoke to avoid direct fire while targeting weaker side armour with APDS. A laser warning system alerts the crew to incoming laser-guided missiles. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
jp_type_89b_i_go_otsu: The I-Go was Japan's first mass-produced home-grown tank, and the Otsu model was the world's first mass-produced diesel tank; derived from the Vickers Medium C and adopted in 1929, it was soon reclassified as a medium for weighing over 10 tonnes. It did well against poorly equipped Chinese forces but was too slow for motorised infantry and outgunned at Khalkhin Gol, giving way to the Ha-Go and Chi-Ha. In the game it is a slow, lightly armoured infantry-support tank whose low-velocity 57 mm fires capable HEAT, able to lob shells from behind cover at close range. It is a demanding teacher of positioning and shell arcs. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_90: Japan began the Type 90 straight after adopting the Type 74, since it would have to face the T-72, Leopard 2 and M1 generation; accepted in 1990 to replace the Type 61 and Type 74, it stresses advanced fire control, an onboard computer, automatic target tracking and an autoloader. In the game it resembles a Leopard 2A4 and fires a licence-built Rheinmetall L44-based gun, but differs in key ways. Its 4-second autoloader lets it keep pressure on enemy tanks even when shots do not kill, a laser warning system adds awareness, and a very powerful engine makes it one of the faster MBTs, able to keep pace with lighter vehicles. It was introduced in Update 1.79 "Project X".
jp_type_90b: The Type 90 (B) is the version of Japan's Type 90 fitted to carry the Type 92 mine-clearing roller, whose mounting points rule out the dozer blade of the standard tank. In the game it is effectively a spare Type 90, with the same fast 4-second autoloaded 120 mm firing JM33, strong mobility and middling armour for an MBT. The only real change is the 10 mm mounting plates on the lower front hull, which is why it cannot take a dozer blade. It was introduced in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
jp_type_90b_camo: This Type 90 (B) represents the 3rd Company of the Fuji Tank Instructor Corps, which trains new JGSDF tank crews on the type's autoloader, hydropneumatic suspension and electronics. In the game it behaves just like other Type 90s: a 4-second reload, suspension that tilts the hull to help gun angles, a thermal sight, laser rangefinder and laser warning, and a strong engine on a lightly armoured body, all suiting flanking or hull-down sniping followed by a change of position. Its extra hull plates add little protection and prevent fitting a dozer blade. It was introduced in the "Alpha Strike" update.
jp_type_90b_sm: Development of the Type 90 began soon after the Type 74 to counter the T-72; production tanks used a Japanese 120 mm smoothbore instead of the Rheinmetall L/44 to cut costs, and 341 were built from 1990 to 2009, all still in service, with the (B) adding mounts for the Type 92 mine roller. This version, from the 2026 Senrai Maidens event, is styled after the character Usagi but otherwise matches the other premium Type 90 (B). It is fast and agile with a quick autoloader, but its armour cannot reliably stop most shells; blow-out panels protect against hits on turret-rear ammunition, and the adjustable suspension helps on rough ground and with gun angles. It has extra 10 mm front plates and no dozer blade.
jp_type_93: The Type 93 mounts Type 91 surface-to-air missiles on a Toyota Mega Cruiser (BXD10) light vehicle, replacing 35 mm Oerlikon gun emplacements and Type 87s as a fast-reacting air-defence unit. In the game it reaches top speed easily and can slip behind friendly tanks to cover them from aircraft. It has no radar and can only fire once a target is locked, so it is practically useless against ground vehicles and should avoid them. Thermal sights, a small size and nimble handling also make it an excellent scout. It was introduced in the "Starfighters" update.
jp_type_94: The Type 94 truck with a Type 98 20 mm cannon on its bed was a simple way to motorise air defence for tank and infantry units, letting the gun fire without first being unhitched; wheels for the mount were carried behind the cab so it could be set down when needed. In the game it is fragile like any truck, with only three crew, so it should stay away from the front despite being a capable light anti-tank gun. The 20 mm, with 20-round magazines, up to 45 mm of penetration and good traverse and reload, shreds aircraft and light vehicles, and it introduces the gun used on the next two Japanese anti-aircraft vehicles. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_95_ha_go: The Ha-Go was designed because the I-Go could not keep up with motorised infantry moving at 40 km/h; finalised in 1935, it served as the army's main tank until the Chi-Ha and, being light and cheap, became Japan's most numerous wartime tank. In the game it is small and nimble, best supporting larger tanks from the flanks, but its thin armour falls to cannons and autocannons alike. Using its gun depression to fight from behind terrain with only the turret exposed gets the most from it. It came with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai", and since Update 1.85 "Supersonic" it is no longer a reserve tank, unlocking only after reaching rank II.
jp_type_95_ha_go_commander: Before radios were widespread, Japanese company commanders' Ha-Gos were often given distinctive paint or insignia so they could be seen, and some carried radios or, as here, smoke dischargers. In the game it shares the Ha-Go's agility and thin armour, working as a support tank that helps heavier vehicles advance. Four smoke grenades are the difference, giving it the option of a covered approach or retreat. It came with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai" and was the prize in the 2016 "Christmas gift" giveaway.
jp_type_95_heavy: The Ro-Go was Japan's take on the multi-turreted heavy tank fashion of the T-28, T-35 and Independent, and the second Japanese tank adopted after the I-Go; trials in Manchuria exposed problems with cost, production, weight and mobility, so it was never mass-produced. In the game it plays much like the I-Go, with almost no real armour, sluggish mobility and a low-velocity main gun with a potent HEAT shell. On top of that it adds a 37 mm gun in a secondary turret, a rear machine gun with its own crewman and a larger crew overall, which helps survivability. It was introduced in Update 1.67 "Assault".
jp_type_95_so_ki: After the single-gun Ta-Se was rejected for poor accuracy, cramped crew conditions and difficulty sustaining fire, the So-Ki tried again on the Ke-Ni chassis with twin 20 mm cannons behind only a gun shield, adding firepower while lightening traverse and freeing room for the gunner. In the game its twin 20 mm guns fire high-velocity rounds and traverse well, and the Ke-Ni chassis makes it quick. It can scout by shooting and marking tanks, but its main job is protecting the team from aircraft, and in skilled hands it stays competitive against planes even at higher tiers. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_97_chi_ha: Mitsubishi's Chi-Ha was meant to replace the I-Go with what was essentially a four-man Ha-Go carrying a gun with more explosive power than the 37 mm; it beat the cheaper Osaka Arsenal Chi-Ni because the outbreak of war with China freed up budget, and it became Japan's main medium tank and the basis of many variants. In the game it is basically a better-armoured, better-engined I-Go and can seem mediocre, but played to its strengths it does well: decent mobility and a low-velocity gun whose fairly high-penetration HEAT shell can be lobbed over cover. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_97_chi_ha_12cm: The Chi-Ha Short Gun was a Navy conversion that placed a short 120 mm naval gun in a modified Chi-Ha Kai turret, meant to defend naval bases and support infantry in home defence, much like the Army's Ho-I. In the game the 120 mm destroys most enemies in one hit and wrecks the lightest targets even with near misses. A roughly 10-second reload, sluggish turret and slow shells make it awkward to aim, and armoured targets call for shots that splash the explosive onto their roofs or lower hulls. It was a pre-order premium pack when the Japanese ground tree launched in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_97_kai: Defeat at Khalkhin Gol in 1939 showed the limits of the infantry-support Chi-Ha's low-velocity 57 mm, so the higher-velocity Type 1 47 mm was fitted in the Shinhōtō turret to create the Chi-Ha Kai. It did well against light Allied armour early in the Pacific War, in Malaya and at Corregidor, but was outclassed by tanks like the M4 Sherman. In the game it is the first proper Japanese tank-fighter, with a higher-velocity gun, punchy post-penetration damage and an extra crewman over the Chi-Ha, whose mobility it keeps. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_97_kai_td: This Chi-Ha Kai was a Twitch drop for viewers of the Japan Tournament 2021 on 3 April and has been unobtainable since; it differs from the standard tank only in its default camouflage. The Chi-Ha Kai paired the Shinhōtō turret with the higher-velocity Type 1 47 mm after Khalkhin Gol exposed the original Chi-Ha's weak gun, and it served well against light Allied armour early in the Pacific War before the Sherman outclassed it. In the game it keeps the Chi-Ha's mobility while adding a better gun with dangerous post-penetration effect and an extra crew member.
jp_type_98_ke_ni: The Ke-Ni was a light tank prototype meant to improve on the Ha-Go with a smaller silhouette, better armour and Christie suspension; with only a driver in the hull, its machine gun moved to a coaxial turret mount, unusual for a Japanese tank. High command saw no need to replace the Ha-Go, which was coping with the little armour China fielded. In the game it is small and fast, playing much like the M22; the gun is not top-class, but APHE does useful damage after penetrating, so flanking shots into enemy sides suit it. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_98_ta_se: The Ta-Se was a prototype to put the Type 98 20 mm cannon on a tracked chassis for armoured companies, but the simpler Type 94 truck took priority, and the army decided towed or truck-mounted guns were easier than mass-producing anti-aircraft tanks. In the game it destroys aircraft and light tanks alike, and quickly. Built on the Ke-Ni chassis, it shares that tank's nimble handling and thin armour. Two of its three crew are exposed in the turret, but unlike the two-man German Flakpanzer I and Flakpanzer 38, it can sometimes lose one and keep fighting. It arrived with the first Japanese ground tree in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
jp_type_99: Planned from 1985 to replace the short-barrelled Type 75, the Type 99 pairs an MHI hull lengthened from the future Type 89 IFV chassis with a JSW 155 mm L/52 howitzer; trials ran from 1996 to 1998, but its high price means it will share the replacement task with the wheeled Type 19. In the game its long barrel gives shells a remarkable 940 m/s, with fairly quick traverse and an autoloader for faster reloading. The engine is underpowered for its bulk, and the long-nosed vehicle is easy to spot from afar. It was introduced in the "Air Superiority" update.
ju-188a-2: The Ju 188 grew from Junkers' repeated upgrades of the Ju 88 once the Ju 288 proved far from ready, adding stronger defensive armament and airframe changes; the A series used Jumo 213 engines, while the E took the BMW 801. Though conceived as a fast light bomber, it carries up to 3,000 kg of bombs, yet it has no bombsight. A structural limit of 675 km/h lets it dive quickly onto bases for accurate drops, and five defensive positions with 7.92 mm machine guns and 20 mm cannons protect it. It was introduced in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
ju-288c: Junkers' Ju 288 was the favoured entry in the Luftwaffe's Bomber B contest for a fast Ju 88 replacement, offering a pressurised cabin, higher speed and altitude, longer range, strong defences and a far bigger bomb load; failure of the Jumo 222 engine and complex landing gear meant only a handful of prototypes, and the final C batch used the He 177's coupled DB 610 engines. In the game it is the ultimate fast bomber, combining speed, acceleration, strong defensive guns and a huge payload: two 2,500 kg bombs can wipe out vehicle groups or threaten a battleship, while 36 × 50 kg bombs can destroy up to two bases or carpet-bomb. It was introduced in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
ju-388j: The Ju 388, last of the Ju 88 line, was built for high-altitude work in reconnaissance, bomber and fighter versions; only three of this J fighter were made before news that B-29s were going to the Pacific shifted production to the K. It carried a remote rear turret with twin 13 mm MG 131s, two MK 108s and two MG 151s firing forwards, two more upward-firing Schräge Musik MG 151s, turbocharged BMW 801TJ engines and a nose radar. In the game its Ju 88 roots show: handling is poor, performance lacklustre and climbing to its best altitude hard, so it should fly with teammates. It was a premium reward for the "Battlefield Engineer" event in Update 1.87 "Locked On" and is now available only through the Marketplace.
ju-87b-2: The Stuka grew from Junkers designer Hermann Pohlmann's faith in dive bombing, backed by the Luftwaffe's Ernst Udet; from the B-1 it carried the "Jericho trumpet" sirens, which helped pilots judge dive speed and frightened those below, and the B-2, of which 225 were built, added hydraulic cowling flaps and fittings for tropical and winter use. In the game it is the German tree's first Stuka, with an outstanding payload for its rank of up to 1,200 kg, including a single 1,000 kg bomb. It dives fast and pulls out safely, but level speed and manoeuvrability are poor, so close support is its real strength, one that keeps it useful at higher tiers. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87d-3: The Ju 87 D-3 is a German dive bomber that is slow in level flight but gathers speed quickly in a dive, where air brakes keep it from overshooting into the ground. It soaks up a fair amount of 7.7 mm and 12.7 mm fire, and its low stall speed and good low-speed handling help both on bombing runs and in turning fights. Two wing MG 17s deal with soft targets such as armoured cars and anti-aircraft guns, while its bombs handle tanks, pillboxes, ships and bases; the twin MG 81 rear guns fire fast but rarely bring fighters down. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87d-3_italy: Italy's Ju 87 D-3 mirrors the German version: sluggish in level flight but quick in a dive, with air brakes to control the descent. It is sturdy enough to absorb a good deal of rifle-calibre and 12.7 mm fire, and a low stall speed gives it agility at low speed for diving attacks or the odd turning fight. The two MG 17s in the wings suit soft targets like armoured cars and anti-aircraft guns, the bomb load takes care of tanks, pillboxes, ships and bases, and the rear twin MG 81s fire rapidly but lack killing power. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
ju-87d-5: Combat showed the Ju 87's protection was lacking, and adding armour and bombs to the D-3 hurt its handling, so the D-5 gained a wingspan 0.6 m longer, a strengthened cockpit floor window, two MG 151/20 cannons and an extra aileron hinge for higher dive speeds; 1,178 were built, entering combat in the USSR in summer 1943 before Fw 190 strike variants took over. In the game it is a dedicated striker: slow and a poor climber, especially when loaded, but agile at all speeds and able to dive and recover cleanly, though it bleeds speed fast in manoeuvres. Strong guns and bombs are its assets; its armour counts for little when it can neither outrun attackers nor fight them off. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87g_1: The Ju 87 G-1 mounts a pair of 37 mm BK 3,7 cannons on an early D-series Stuka, using the D-3's wing where the G-2 takes the D-5's, and the type was highly rated by Hans-Ulrich Rudel. In the game it is among the deadliest ground-attack aircraft: high-velocity armour-piercing 37 mm rounds destroy most tanks, and with the right belt aircraft too, though the armoured-target belt does little to planes and the air-target belt little to armour. Each cannon holds only 12 rounds, which caps how much damage it can do per sortie. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87g_2: The G-2 is the cannon-armed Stuka built on the later Ju 87 D-5 airframe, with its larger wing area, where the G-1 used the D-3's wing; its flight model in the game is otherwise the same as the G-1's. Its two 37 mm BK 3,7 cannons, a weapon favoured by Hans-Ulrich Rudel, fire high-velocity armour-piercing rounds that make it one of the most lethal tank hunters in the game, and they can kill aircraft too with the proper belt. Choosing the belt matters, since each type is poor against the other kind of target, and only 12 rounds per gun limit how much it can destroy before rearming. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87r-2: The Ju 87 R was a long-range Stuka for anti-shipping work, carrying more fuel at the cost of payload when fully fuelled; the main R-2 production model added a stronger airframe for faster dives and an improved Jumo 211, and around 800 served until the war's end. In the game it gives up wing bomb racks and the "Jericho trumpet" sirens, but handles better, particularly in high-speed dives, and is less vulnerable than the B-2. Mediocre at anything else, it excels at precise dive-bombing and stays useful against ground targets even at higher tiers. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-87r-2_italy: Italy's Ju 87 R-2 is close to the German aircraft but differs slightly in speed and flight performance and, more noticeably, in payload: it cannot carry the 1,000 kg bomb but can hang 50 kg bombs under the wings. Two forward 7.92 mm machine guns match most fighters of its rank, and the gunner's single 7.92 mm in the rear, despite its blind spots, can discourage some pursuers. It was introduced in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
ju-87r-2_snake: Stukas sent to North Africa with Rommel's Afrika Korps supported Axis offensives at Tobruk and El Alamein and attacked Allied convoys, succeeding in 1941–42 until more capable Allied fighter-bombers and air superiority drove the survivors back to Europe in 1943. This R-2 represents that campaign and plays like the standard long-range Stuka: no wing bomb racks or sirens, but better handling, especially in fast dives, and less vulnerability than earlier versions. It is weak outside its speciality, yet precise dive-bombing keeps it effective against ground targets at higher tiers. It was introduced in the "Danger Zone" update.
ju-88a-1: Junkers won the Reich Air Ministry's 1935 fast-bomber competition with the Ju 88, first flown in December 1936; a 1937 demand for dive-bombing ability forced structural strengthening, and the A-1 entered production in mid-1939, with 1,270 built and widely used early in the war. In the game it is agile and fast for a bomber and carries a respectable bomb load. Its defensive guns cannot reliably fend off fighters, though, and with no armour the crew is very exposed. It was introduced in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
ju-88a-4: The Ju 88 A-4 was the most produced Ju 88 bomber, with 2,332 built from 1940, adding a longer wingspan, more defensive guns, a stronger airframe and Jumo 211J engines; it fought from Britain to the Mediterranean and the Soviet Union and spawned reconnaissance and heavy fighter versions. In the game the stronger engines give it more speed and payload than the A-1, otherwise keeping the type's good agility, high speed and useful bomb load. Defensive armament remains weak. It has been in the game since open beta, before Update 1.27.
ju-88a-4_finland: Finland bought 24 Ju 88 A-4s in April 1943 for No. 44 Squadron, already experienced with twin-engine bombers, but crews found the aircraft complicated and spent most of that year training, flying only a few raids. In the Swedish tree it plays like the German A-4: fast for a bomber, with air brakes to shed speed, and equally adept at dive and level bombing. A 2,400 kg payload can destroy bases in air battles, and the defensive guns can down some interceptors, but there is no ventral gunner to cover the blind spot below, and forward firepower is a single light machine gun. It was introduced in the "Fire and Ice" update.
ka_29: The Ka-29 is an assault version of the Ka-27 naval helicopter, with Kamov's coaxial rotors and the boxy cabin of its anti-submarine and rescue parent, adapted to carry a 2A42 cannon, Shturm missiles, rockets and gun pods; over 60 were built from the late 1980s, laid up after the Soviet collapse and largely reactivated around 2020. In the game it handles differently from the Hinds but carries much of the Mi-24P's weaponry, making it a good introduction to coaxial-rotor flying and the offset 2A42 before the Ka-52. Limited ordnance, decent agility and the lethal cannon favour fairly aggressive play, while hovering too long risks a vortex-induced crash. It was introduced in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
ka_50: Developed in the 1980s from the V-80 to complement helicopters like the Mi-24, the Ka-50 is a single-seat anti-tank helicopter whose coaxial rotors give it stability, precision and agility, backed by advanced sensors, guided missiles and a 30 mm cannon. In the game a tough airframe and strong weapon options allow many styles of play, and its standout weapon is the 9K127 Vikhr missile, which lets it hit targets from long range. It was introduced as a premium pack in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
ka_52: While the Ka-50 competed with the Mi-28 in the 1980s, Kamov devised a two-seat battlefield support version with side-by-side seating, extra wing hardpoints, an air-to-ground radar and a day/night thermal sight; to keep performance, cockpit armour and cannon ammunition were cut and a new VK-2500 engine fitted, and production followed trials completed in 2008. In the game it keeps the Ka-50's long-range, proximity-fused Vikhr missiles and fine flight performance with better electronics. A 2A42 cannon with strong APDS and SO-13OF rockets that usually destroy a tank in one hit complete a well-rounded helicopter that can threaten aircraft too, one of the best in the game. It was introduced in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
kfir_c10_colombia: The Kfir C.10 is IAI's export modernisation of the Kfir, flown solely by Colombia since 2009, with an Elta AESA radar, a cockpit rebuilt around two multifunction displays and Elbit's DASH helmet sight for off-boresight shots. In the game it keeps the C.7's flight performance, nose authority and acceleration, outturning and outrunning many opponents, and its radar scans faster than non-AESA sets. DERBY active radar missiles are a big step up but are outranged beyond about 12–16 km by the AIM-120 and PL-12, and only four are carried. Fighters such as the F-16 or Gripen hold energy better, so it suits leading attacks in downtiers and supporting in uptiers. It was a Winter Tales 2024 reward in the "Storm Warning" update.
kfir_c2: Israel built the Kfir by fitting its Nesher (Mirage 5) design with new avionics and the F-4 Phantom's GE J79, which required a reshaped rear fuselage and bigger intakes; the prototype flew in June 1973 and the C.1 entered service in 1975, followed by the C.2, which added large canards, revised wing leading edges and nose strakes after complaints about agility. In the game it is a versatile fighter-bomber in the Mirage 5 mould, turning well enough to bring guns or missiles to bear, though it carries only two IR missiles. Up to eight 1,000 lb bombs and CCIP/CCRP computing let it destroy a base or several tanks. It was a reward for the "Battle for Arachis" event in the "Wind of Change" update.
kfir_c7: The C.7 was the final and most advanced Kfir, with larger canards, a more powerful J79 for heavier take-offs and extra hardpoints; overshadowed by the F-15 and F-16, it scored its only air-to-air kill in 1993 during Operation Accountability, while export aircraft went to Colombia, Ecuador and Sri Lanka. In the game it accelerates faster than MiG-21s and even the F-16C and MiG-29SMT, and the Python 3 is an extremely agile, quick missile. It has no radar-guided missiles, only a ranging radar for the gunsight, and no guided ground weapons, but carries plenty of bombs and rockets, and its DEFA 30 mm guns hit hard and are easy to aim. It was introduced in the "Winged Lions" update.
kfir_canard: The Kfir Canard, or Kfir Gderot, was an interim upgrade of the original Kfir, the J79-powered development of IAI's Nesher that flew in 1973; pilots found it less agile than the Mirage III, so small canards were added to the intakes. Besides serving Israel mainly as a ground attacker, it was leased to the US Navy and Marine Corps as the F-21A to stand in for MiG-23s in aggressor training. In the game it resembles the Nesher with fixed canards, but its air-to-air weapons trail its opponents' and it suffers the usual delta-wing limits. American bombs and rocket pods make it effective against grouped ground targets. It was introduced in the "Apex Predators" update.
